raw: वनवासम् न जानामि रामस्यहम् महात्मनः । विवासनम् वा सौमित्रेः सीतायाश्च यथाभवत् ॥२-७५-४॥
translation: I knew nothing of the banishment of great Rama nor did I know how Lakshmana or Sita had gone on exile.

raw: त्वया तस्य निरस्तस्य पीडितस्य विशेषतः । इह एत्य पुनर् आह्वानम् शंकाम् जनयति इव मे ॥४-१५-११॥
translation: 'One who is defeated and badly mauled by you is again coming and inviting you to a duel in this manner arouses suspicion in me.

raw: श्रुत्वा दधिमुखस्येदं सुग्रीवस्तु प्रहृष्य च । वनपालं पुनर्वाक्यं सुग्रीवः प्रत्यभाषत ॥५-६३-२६॥
translation: Beautifulnecked Sugriva heard Dadhimukha, the protector of the garden, felt very glad and replied:

raw: ताम् क्लिष्ट माल्य आभरणाम् विलपन्तीम् अनाथवत् । अभ्यधावत वैदेहीम् रावणो राक्षस अधिपः ॥३-५२-६॥
translation: Ravana, king of the demons, ran towards Sita who was weeping like an orphan with her garlands and ornaments crushed.

raw: ततः पर्वत शृंग आभः तीक्ष्ण तुण्डः खग उत्तमः । वनस्पति गतः श्रीमान् व्याजहार शुभाम् गिरम् ॥३-५०-२॥
translation: Glorious Jatayu, the best among the birds, looked like the peak of a mountain. His beak was sharp. His words were auspious. He spoke from the top of the tree:

raw: राक्षसास्तम् प्लवङ्गानाम् शुश्रुवुस्तेऽपि गर्जितम् । वर्दतामिव दृप्तानाम् मेघानामम्बरे स्वनम् ॥६-२४-५॥
translation: Even the Rakshasas heard the roaring of Vanaras in their pride that was bellowing like that of clouds in the sky.

raw: यत्नवान् च स दुष्टात्मा मद् विनाशाय राघव । बहुशः तत् प्रयुक्ताः च वानरा निहता मया ॥४-८-३४॥
translation: 'O Rama this evilminded one made several attempts to kill me. The monkeys he sent to kill me were themselves killed.

raw: अपश्यत् विमलम् छत्रम् चित्र माल्य उपशोभितम् । चामर व्यजने च अग्र्ये रुक्म दण्डे महाधने ॥३-५-९॥
translation: Rama saw a pure white umbrella with a highly expensive golden staff, decorated with variegated flower garlands.While near his (Indra's) head stood a pair of exquisite ladies with fans made of yak's tail.

raw: एवमुक्त्वा तु तान् सर्वान् राक्षसान् परिपार्श्वतः । यूथपानपि तान् सर्वांस्ताडयामास रावणिः ॥६-४६-१८॥
translation: Indrajith, having spoken in that way to all Rakshasas, began to strike all the Vanara leaders looking at him.

raw: अब्रवीच्च तदा वृत्तं तेषां मध्ये स राघवः । दुर्वासोभिगमं चैव प्रतिज्ञां तापसस्य च ॥७-१०६-६॥
translation: Then, in their midst, Rama recounted the incident, including the arrival of Durvasa and the ascetic's vow.

raw: व्यरोचत तदा तोयम् निर्मलम् गत कल्मषम् । तत्र ऋषि गण गन्धर्वा वसुधा तल वासिनः भव अंग पतितम् तोयम् पवित्रम् इति पस्पृशुः । शापात् प्रपतिता ये च गगनात् वसुधा तलम् ॥१-४३-२६॥
विरूपाक्षः स्वकं नाम धन्वी विश्राव्य राक्षसः । रथादाप्लुत्य दुर्धर्षो गजस्कन्धमुपारुहत् ॥६-९७-१४॥
translation: And thereafter, all the Rakshasas shattered by Sugriva, tormented, fallen on the ground were shouting. Seeing that Virupaksha, himself, who is difficult to encounter, holding his bow, announcing his name, jumped from the chariot onto an elephant in a rut.

raw: तेन चैव तदा तुल्यं सहासीनाः सभासदः । आसनेभ्यः समुत्तस्थुः पूजयन्तः पुरोहितम् ॥२-५-२४॥
translation: All those present in the assembly with him (the king) also got up from their seats as he (Dasaratha) did and paid their obeisance to Vasistha.

raw: सो ऽभिगम्य महात्मानं ज्ञात्वा ऽपि ध्यानमास्थितम् । प्रणतश्च प्रहृष्टश्च प्राप्तं सीतां न्यवेदयत् ॥६-११७-१५॥
translation: Knowing that Sita reached also, great Rama was seen in a meditative mood absorbed in thought. Vibheeshana announced saying, 'Sita has been brought' and greeted with folded palms, full of joy.

raw: पूजितो अहम् त्वया ब्रह्मन् पूज अर्हेण सुसत्कृतः । श्रूयताम् अभिधास्यामि वाक्यम् वाक्य विशारद ॥१-५३-८॥
translation: "O Brahman you are worthy of worship. I was received with reverence and wellentertained by you. O Sage conversant with speech listen.

raw: सुवर्णश्रुङ्गा स्सम्पन्ना स्सवत्सा: कांस्यदोहना: । गवां शतसहस्राणि चत्वारि पुरुषर्षभ: वित्तमन्यच्च सुबहुद्विजेभ्यो रघुनन्दन: । ददौ गोदानमुद्दिश्य पुत्राणां पुत्रवत्सल: ॥१-७२-२३॥
translation: Great among men and affectionate towards his children, (king Dasaratha), the delight of the Raghus donated in the name of his sons' donates to the brahmins four hundred thousand cows. They were capable of abundance of milk. Their horns were plaited with gold. They were accompanied by calves. With them were given away bellmetal vessels for keeping milk and innumerable valuables.

raw: न च प्रार्थयते कश्चिन् मनसा अपि वसुम्धराम् । वने अपि वसतः तस्य बाहु वीर्य अभिरक्षिताम् ॥२-८८-२३॥
translation: No one, even in thought, would ever desire this kingdom, protected by the strength of his arms even while residing in the forest.

raw: व्यक्तं रामोऽभिषेकार्थमिहायास्यति धर्मवित् । इति सूतो मतिं कृत्वा हर्षेण महता वृतः ॥२-१४-६६॥
तद्वृत्तं नृपति श्शृत्वा दूतश्रेष्ठैर्महाबलै: । अज्ञायाऽथ नरेन्द्रस्य आजगाम कुशध्वज: ॥१-७०-८॥
translation: Kusadhwaja having heard the events from the loyal, mighty messengers set out for Mithila in compliance with the request of the king (Janaka).

raw: इन्द्रमेवं ब्रुवाणं तं मान्धाता वाक्यमब्रवीत् । क्व मे शक्र प्रतिहतं शासनं पृथिवीतले ॥७-६७-१२॥
translation: To Indra, who was speaking thus, Mandhata replied, "O Indra, where on the surface of the earth is my rule obstructed?"

raw: यदैवनगरींलङ्कांदुष्प्रवेशांसुरैरपि । प्रविष्टोहनुमान्वीर्यात्तदैवव्यथितावयम् ॥६-११४-१०॥
translation: "To Lanka, which is inaccessible to anyone, Hanuman entered by increasing his valour. Knowing this we worried (that Rama may not be mere mortal)."

raw: अनन्तरं स राजर्षिर्निमिरिक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः । अत्रिमङ्गिरसं चैव भृगुं चैव तपोधनम् ॥७-५५-९॥
translation: Subsequently, the royal sage Nimi, a descendant of Ikshvaku, approached Atri, Angiras, and Bhrigu, who were rich in penance.

raw: यम् अहम् त्वत् कृते पुत्र तम् आधास्ये जय उत्सुकम् । त्रैलोक्य विजयम् पुत्र सह भोक्ष्यसि विज्वरः ॥१-४६-१४॥
translation: O Child I'll create in him eagerness victory. Together with him you will gain victory over the three worlds. Relieved of sorrows, enjoy you'll with him".

raw: अयोनिजां हि मां ज्ञात्वा नाध्यगच्छद्विचिन्तयन् । सदृशं चानुरूपं च महीपाल: पतिं मम ॥२-११८-३७॥
translation: The ruler of the earth knew that I was not born from a woman's womb, and could not find a suitable husband for me after deep reflection.

raw: वर आयुध धरम् रामम् द्रष्टुम् स ऋषि गणाः सुराः । पितामहम् पुरस्कृत्य समेताः तत्र सर्वशः ॥१-७६-९॥
translation: The gods with the Grandsire, Brahma in the forefront, accompanied by sages in groups assembled there to see Rama holding that mighty bow. Gandharvas, apsaras, siddhas, charanas, kinnaras, yakshas, rakshsas and nagas also came there to witness that great wonder.

raw: दुहिता जनकस्य अहम् मैथिलस्य महात्मनः । सीता नाम्ना अस्मि भद्रम् ते रामस्य महिषी प्रिया ॥३-४७-३॥
translation: O best of brahmins be pleased to know I am Sita by name, daughter of the great Janaka, king of Mithila and wife of Rama.

raw: गजश्च गिरिसङ्काशो गवयश्च महाबलः । गवाक्षश्चाग्रतो यातु गवां दृप्तइवर्षभ: ॥६-४-१५॥
translation: "Gaja who is like a mountain in form, Gavaya, the mighty strong and Gavaksha would go like proud bulls that lead the cows".

raw: वाक्यवज्रैरनुपमैर्निर्भिन्दन्निव चाशुगैः । कैकेय्या सर्वमर्माणि सुमन्त्रः प्रत्यभाषत ॥२-३५-४॥
translation: Overcome with anger, charioteer Sumantra started shaking his head and sighing off and on, crushing his palms and grinding his teeth. His eyes turned red due to anger. Overcome with a sudden, ominous grief, the complexion of his face turned red. Sumantra understood the mind of Dasaratha. With sharp arrows of words as if piercing the heart of Kaikeyi, he denounced her in exceptionally harsh words which, like thunderbolt, cut her to the quick:

raw: राजा दशरथो नाम रथकुञ्जरवाजिमान् । पुण्यशीलो महाकीर्तिर्ऋजुरासीन्महायशाः ॥५-३१-२॥
translation: "There was an illustrious king called Dasaratha in Ikshvaku race, a master of chariots, elephants and horses. He was highly meritorious and renowned.

raw: मायया मम वत्सेन वञ्चनार्थं वनौकसाम् । किञ्चिदेव हतं तत्र सीतेयमिति दर्शितम् ॥६-९३-३६॥
translation: 'My son showed the Vanaras there something which had been killed there to hoodwink as Sita."

raw: स्वानि राज्यानि मुख्यानि ऋद्धानि मुदितानि च । समृद्धधनधान्यानि पूर्णानि वसुमन्ति च ॥७-३९-७॥
translation: Their own excellent and prosperous kingdoms were joyful, full of abundant wealth and grain, and rich in resources.

raw: पादुके ते पुरस्कृत्य शासन्तं वै वसुन्धराम् । चातुर्वर्ण्यस्य लोकस्य त्रातारं सर्वतो भयात् ॥६-१२८-३१॥
translation: ' At a distance of two miles from Ayodhya, Hanuman saw Bharata living in a hermitage wearing black skin of antelope, emaciated, piteous, not clean, without any cleaning of the body, affected by the separation from brother living on fruits and roots, subdued practicing austerities, following righteous practices disciplined, soul purified by meditation, like Brahmarshi in brilliance, placing your sandals on ground ruling the earth, all the four divisions free from fear on all sides, protecting the upright, ministers, priests, united with chiefs of army stood there' (reported Hanuman).

raw: हतप्रवीरा व्यथिता राक्षसेन्द्रचमूस्तदा । जगामाभिमुखी सा तु कुम्भकर्णसुतो यतः ॥६-७६-३५॥
translation: Then many heroes died, Rakshasa king's army was distressed and went towards where Kumbhakarna's son was fighting.

raw: नक्षत्रेषु प्रशस्तेषु मुहूर्तेषु च तद्विदः । निवेशम् स्थापयाम् आसुर् भरतस्य महात्मनः ॥२-८०-१७॥
translation: Men wellversed in the study of planetary positions relating to auspicious constellations and auspicious times arranged different restingplaces at different times during the sojourn of great Bharata.

raw: सिक्तराजपथां कृत्स्नां प्रकीर्णकुसुमोत्कराम् । अयोध्यां मन्थरा तस्मात्प्रासादादन्ववैक्षत ॥२-७-२॥
translation: Manthara beheld from that palace the whole of Ayodhya with its highways sprinkled with water and strewn with a lot of flowers.

raw: ततो रक्षो महानादान्मुक्त्वा हन्ति स्म वारुणान् । नानाप्रहरणोपेतैर्धारापातैरिवाम्बुदः ॥७-२३-४८॥
translation: Then, the Rakshasa Ravana, having uttered great roars, struck down the followers of Varuna (Devas) with showers of various weapons, just like a cloud pours down torrents of rain.

raw: आघूर्णित तरन्ग ओघः सम्ब्भ्रान्त उरग राक्षसः । उद्वर्तित महाग्राहः सम्वृत्तः सलिल आशयः ॥६-२१-३२॥
translation: The waves rose up tossing and whirling about. The agitated Nagas and Rakshasas were thrown up by a highly disturbed ocean that produced a great sound.

raw: युक्तःपरमसंविग्नोराक्षर्भहुभिर्वृतः । उत्तरंनगरद्वारंरावणस्स्वयमास्थितः ॥६-३७-१३॥
translation: "Ravana himself stands at the north gate of Lanka, highly agitated surrounded by many thousands of Rakshasas wielding weapons."

raw: दीप्तपावक सङ्काशैः शरैः काञ्चनभूषणैः । निर्बिभेद रणे रामो दशग्रीवं समाहितम् ॥६-१०३-४॥
translation: Sri Rama steadily covered Ravana, the ten headed Rakshasa with shining shafts covered with gold glowing like fire in the battle.

raw: चपलस्येह कृत्यानि सहसानुप्रधावतः । छिद्रमन्ये प्रपद्यन्ते क्रौञ्चस्य स्वमिव द्विजाः ॥६-६३-१९॥
translation: "Enemies find out the weakness of the king who is unsteady and rush after the actions forcibly without thinking like brahmins just as birds find the holes in Krauncha mountain and elaborate to others."

raw: एवमुक्ताः सुसंहृष्टा वायुपुत्रेण वानराः । शैलशृङ्गाण्यगांश्चैव जगृहुर्हृष्टमानसाः ॥६-८२-५॥
translation: Wise son of wind god having spoken in that way, delighted in mind the Vanaras seized peaks of mountains and also trees in great fury.

raw: द्वौ च खड्गौ रथगतौ पार्श्वस्थौ पार्श्वशोभितौ । चतुर्हस्तत्सरुयुतौ व्यक्तहस्तदशायतौ ॥६-७१-२१॥
translation: "It has two swords off our cubits and ten cubits long swords provided with hilts hanging on its sides as decoration."

raw: दिशः तस्याः ततो भूयः प्रस्थितो दक्षिणम् दिशम् । विन्ध्य पादप संकीर्णाम् चन्दन द्रुम शोभिताम् ॥४-४६-१७॥
translation: 'Then chased by Vali, I changed my present direction from the east towards the southern quarter where Vindhya mountain stood with its, beautiful sandal trees.

raw: युधाजित्तु तथेत्याह गमनं प्रति राघवम् । रत्नानि च धनं चैव त्वय्येवाक्षय्यमस्त्विति ॥७-३८-१३॥
translation: Yudhājit then said to Rama regarding his departure, "So be it; let the jewels and wealth indeed be inexhaustible in you alone."

raw: पितरम् चानुशोचामि मातरम् च यशस्विनीम् । अपि वानौध भवेताम् तु रुदन्तौ तावभीक्ष्णशः ॥२-४६-६॥
translation: What distresses me is the thought that both father and illustrious mother may become blind by repeated weeping (over us).

raw: दीप्तशूलगदाखड्गप्रासतोमरकार्मुकम् । तद्राक्षसबलं घोरं भीमविक्रमपौरुषम् ॥६-७५-५४॥
स चिन्तया दुस्सहया परीतम्विसंज्ञम् एकम् विजने मनस्वी । भ्रातुर् विषादात् त्वरितो अति दीनःसमीक्ष्य सौमित्रिः उवाच रामम् ॥४-३०-१५॥
translation: Observing Rama who had lost his senses, lying alone in unbearable agony, venerable Lakshmana became sad and miserable and spoke to his brother:

raw: धनुर्ग्रहवरो यस्य बाणखड्गास्त्रभृत्स्वयम् । लक्ष्मणोव्रजति ह्यग्रे तस्य किम् नाम दुर्लभम् ॥२-४४-२०॥
translation: What is impossible for Rama ahead of whom moves Lakshmana, the best of archers, weilding swords, arrows and other weapons?

raw: पुरा कृतयुगे राजन्ब्राह्मणा वै तपस्विनः । अब्राह्मणस्तदा राजन्न तपस्वी कथञ्चन ॥७-७४-९॥
translation: O King, in the ancient Krita Yuga, only brahmins were ascetics, and no non-brahmin was an ascetic by any means.

raw: लक्षितेयं मया सीता तथा शोकपायणा । गृह्य यां नाभिजानासि पञ्चास्यामिव पन्नगीम् ॥५-५१-२३॥
translation: "I have seen Sita immersed in deep sorrow. You do not realise that by abducting her you are keeping a fivehooded female serpent in your house.

raw: दीक्षितम् व्रतसम्पन्नम् वराजिनधरम् शुचिम् । कुरङ्गपाणिम् च पश्यन्ती त्वाम् भजाम्यहम् ॥२-१६-२३॥
translation: I shall be delighted to see you initiated and engaged in the observance of the vow made pure, wearing excellent deerskin and carrying the horns of an antelope in your hand.

raw: इत एव पथा क्षिप्रं प्रतिगच्छामि तां पुरीम् । अयोध्यामागतो ह्येष पन्थाः परमदुर्गमः ॥६-१२४-६॥
translation: " As it is very difficult to return to that city, think of the path to depart."

raw: नरान्तकः कुम्भहनुर्महानादः समुन्नतः । प्रहस्तसचिवा ह्येते निर्ययुः परिवार्य तम् ॥६-५७-३१॥
translation: Naranthaka, Kumbhahanu, Mahanada, Samunnatha, the adjutants of Prahastha went with him.

raw: श्रुत्वा सेनापतिं प्राप्तं भरतं केकयाधिपः । युधाजिद्गार्ग्यसहितं परां प्रीतिमुपागमत् ॥७-१०१-१॥
translation: Having heard that Commander Bharata had arrived, the King of Kekaya, accompanied by Yudhajit and Gargya, attained great joy.

raw: यज्ञ विघ्न करी यक्षी पुरा वर्धेत मायया । वध्यताम् तावत् एव एषा पुरा संध्या प्रवर्तते ॥१-२६-२२॥
विलपन्तीम् तथा ताम् तु कौसल्याम् प्रमद उत्तमाम् । इदम् धर्मे स्थिता धर्म्यम् सुमित्रा वाक्यम् अब्रवीत् ॥२-४४-१॥
translation: While Kausalya, the best of women was thus lamenting, virtuous Sumitra spoke to her these righteous words:

raw: गृहीतश्चैव पृष्टश्च काले दृष्ट: सकारण: । कच्चिन्न मुच्यते चोरो धनलोभान्नरर्षभ ॥२-१००-५८॥
translation: O best among men I trust that a thief, caught redhanded and interrogated and has sufficient proof is not set free, out of greed for money.

raw: अत्यर्थं स्वर्गिणं त विमाने रघुनन्दन । उपास्ते ऽप्सरसां वीर सहस्रं दिव्यभूषणम् ॥७-७७-१२॥
translation: O Raghunandana, O hero, a thousand Apsaras adorned with divine ornaments served that exceedingly celestial being in the aerial chariot.

raw: ततो ऽर्धदिवसे प्राप्ते पूज्यमानस्ततस्ततः । अयोध्यां प्राप्य काकुत्स्थो मध्यकक्ष्यामवारुहत् ॥७-८२-१८॥
translation: Then, by midday, Rama, being honored from all sides, reached Ayodhya and descended into the middle chamber of his palace.

raw: कुम्भकर्णोमहानादस्त्रासयन् सर्ववानरान् । शूलंससर्जवैरोषादङ्गदेतुमहाबलः ॥६-६७-४७॥
translation: Mighty Kumbhakarna agitated, making loud noise and frightening all the Vanaras hurled his pike on Angada.

raw: वासमौपयिकम् मन्ये तव राम महाबल । नानानगगणोपेतः किन्नरोरगसेवितह् ॥२-५४-३९॥
translation: O mighty Rama, I think mount Chitrakuta is the right place for you to stay. Go there. That mountain is full of trees of every kind, is inhabited by kinneras and uragas (serpents). It echoes with the cries of peacocks, is frequented by mighty tuskers. Filled with fruits and roots, it is sacred and pleasant.

raw: विश्वामित्रोऽब्रवीत् वाक्यम् शृणु येन बलोत्कटा । वर दान कृतम् वीर्यम् धारयति अबला बलम् ॥१-२५-४॥
translation: Viswamitra said, "Listen, how she acquired the prowess and strength by virtue of a boon she received.

raw: केचिद्रजतसङ्काशा: केचित् क्षतजसन्निभा: । पीतमाञ्जिष्ठवर्णाश्च केचिन्मणिवरप्रभा: ॥२-९४-५॥
translation: This mountain with its peaks is adorned with various minerals. Some of the regions have the radiance of silver and bronze, some look bloodred or maddercrimson, some sparkle like the rarest of gems while others shine like topaz or crystal or a flower of ketaka plant or shimmer like stars and quicksilver.

raw: इति उक्त्वा वचनम् सूतम् सान्त्वयित्वा पुनः पुनः । गुहम् वचनम् अक्लीबम् रामः हेतुमद् अब्रवीत् ॥२-५२-६५॥
translation: Having spoken to the charioteer and consoling him again and again, indefatigable Rama spoke to Guha words full of reasoning:

raw: श्रुत्वा पुष्येण पुत्रस्य यौवराज्याभिषेचनम् । प्राणायामेन पुरुषं ध्यायमाना जनार्दनम् ॥२-४-३३॥
translation: Having heard that installation of her son as heirapparent was planned in Pushya constellation, Kausalya was meditating upon the Supreme Person, Lord Visnu by controlling her breath (Pranayama).

raw: ते स्वामिवचनं सर्वे प्रतिगृह्य महौजसः । समुत्पेतुर्महावेगा हुताशसमतेजसः ॥५-४६-१५॥
translation: Taking King's order, the strong and swift warriors, resplendent as the flame of sacrificial fire sallied forth with their army on chariots, on the back of rutting elephants, some on swift horses equipped with sharp weapons of many kinds.

raw: तान् सर्वान् पीडितान् दृष्ट्वा सुरान् सुरपतिः तदा । गमनाय उपचक्राम दिशम् वरुण पालिताम् ॥१-३६-२४॥
translation: "The god of the gods (Mahesvara), seeing all the devatas humiliated began to depart in the westerly direction presided over by Varuna.

raw: अपत्यम् स्वेषु दारेषु न उत्पदयितुम् अर्हथ । अद्य प्रभृति युष्माकम् अप्रजाः सन्तु पत्नयः ॥१-३६-२१॥
तानर्दयित्वा बाणौघैस्त्रासयित्वा च वानरान् । प्रजहास महाबाहुर्वचनं चेदमब्रवीत् ॥६-४६-२४॥
translation: Indrajith hurt the Vanaras with hails of arrows terrifying them. Then the mighty armed son of Ravana laughed and spoke these words.

raw: वज्रमुष्टिस्तु मैन्देन मुष्टिना निहतो रणे । पपात सरथः साश्वः पुराट्ट इव भूतले ॥६-४३-२८॥
translation: Even Vajramushti fell on the ground struck with the fist by Mainda and the chariot and charioteer fell like the fort.

raw: ते गदाभिर्विचित्राभिः प्राशैः खड्गैः परश्वधैः । अन्योन्यं समरे जघ्नुस्तदा वानरराक्षसाः ॥६-९४-१०॥
translation: The Vanaras and Rakshasas attacked one another with wonderful maces, darts, swords, and axes in war.

raw: तस्यां रजन्यां व्युष्टायां प्रातर्नृपतिबोधकाः । वन्दिनः समुपातिष्ठन्सौम्या नृपतिवेश्मनि ॥७-३७-२॥
translation: As that night dawned, in the morning, gentle bards, who were the awakeners of the king, stood near the king's palace.

raw: अतिमात्रं शरौघेण पीड्यमानौ नरोत्तमौ । तानिषून् पततो भल्लेरनेकैर्निचकृन्ततुः ॥६-८०-३१॥
translation: Brightened by the mass of arrows on their body, the best of men, Rama and Lakshmana began to tear the numerous arrows called Bhallas.

raw: न पश्यामि भयस्थानम् भयम् चैवोपधारये । भ्रष्टश्च स्वरयोगो मे चाया चोपहता मम ॥२-६९-२०॥
translation: I do not see any reason for apprehension but I experience only fear. My voice has degenerated. My appearance looks haggard. Without any reason whatsoever I detest myself.

raw: बालार्काभिमुखो बालो बालार्क इव मूर्तिमान् । ग्रहीतुकामो बालार्कं प्लवते ऽम्बरमध्यगः ॥७-३५-२४॥
translation: The child, facing the morning sun, soared through the middle of the sky like an embodied morning sun, desirous of seizing the sun itself.

raw: विश्वामित्रम् पुरस्कृत्य पितुः पादौ उपस्पृशन् । राजा च राघवौ पुत्रौ निशाम्य परिहर्षितः ॥१-६९-१८॥
क्रीडाम् अनुभविष्यन्ति समेत्य कपि कुन्जराः । सपुत्र दाराः सामात्या भर्तृ व्यसन पीडिताः ॥५-१३-३५॥
भरतात्तु महाबाहोरसितो नाम जायत । यस्यैते प्रतिराजान उदपद्यन्त शत्रव: । हैहयास्तालजङ्घाश्च शूराश्च शशिबिन्दव: ॥२-११०-१५॥
translation: Mightyarmed Bharata had a son named Asita against whom the Haihayas, Talajanghas and the indomitable Sasibindus, the rival kings rose as enenmies.

raw: गायन्ति दिव्यगेयानि वादयन्ति तथा ऽपराः । क्ष्वेलयन्ति तथा चान्या नृत्यन्ति च तथा ऽपराः ॥७-७७-१३॥
translation: Some (celestial women) sing divine songs, others play musical instruments, some engage in playful sports, and still others dance.

raw: सखे शृणुष्व सुग्रीव न त्वया ऽहं विनाकृतः । गच्छेयं देवलोकं वा परमं वा पदं महत् ॥७-१०८-२६॥
translation: "O friend Sugriva, listen," said Rama, "I would not go to the world of gods or to any great supreme abode without you."

raw: कृत्वा तौ सुचिरम् कालम् धर्मिष्ठौ ताः कथाः तदा । मुदा परमया युक्तौ प्रीयेताम् तौ परस्परम् ॥१-५२-११॥
translation: Both the righteous personalities dwelt at length on various matters and interesting anecdotes with great delight and derived mutual pleasure.

raw: पीत्वा तैलं प्रनृत्ताश्च प्रहसन्त्यो महास्वनाः । लङ्कायां भस्मरूक्षायां प्रविष्टा राक्षसस्त्रियः ॥५-२७-३७॥
translation: "All the demonesses in the city of Lanka which had turned dry, reduced to ashes, were dancing, laughing and shouting loudly drunk with oil..

raw: निर्मनुष्याम् इमाम् सर्वाम् अयोध्याम् मनुज ऋषभ । करिष्यामि शरैअः तीक्ष्णैः यदि स्थास्यति विप्रिये ॥२-२१-१०॥
translation: O best of men, if the whole of Ayodhya stands against you I shall depopulate it with my sharp arrows.

raw: उष्यतां चेह रजनी सकाशे मम राघव । प्रभाते पुष्पकेण त्वं गन्ता ऽसि पुरमेव हि ॥७-७६-२८॥
translation: O scion of Raghu, please stay here for the night near me, and in the morning, you will certainly go to your city by the Pushpaka chariot.

raw: तादृशानाम् सहस्रैः ताम् अभि पूर्णाम् महारथैः । पुरीम् आवसयमास राजा दशरथः तदा ॥१-५-२२॥
translation: The city was inhabited by thousands of warriors known as maharathas. They were skilled archers and sharphanded. They would not pierce with arrows, solitary persons, persons without defence, fleeing foes who could be tracked down through hints from sound. With sharp arrows or with the strength of their arms, they would kill roaring and inebriated lions, tigers, boars etc. in the forest. It was in that city (of Ayodhya) that king Dasaratha lived.

raw: हम्सो यथा राजतपञ्जरसथः । सिम्हो यथा मन्दरकन्दरस्थः । वीरो यथा गर्वितकुञ्जरस्थ । श्चन्द्रो विबभ्राज तथामभरस्थः ॥५-५-४॥
translation: 'Like a swan in a cage of silver, like a lion in a cave of Mandara mountain, like a hero on a proud, intoxicated elephant, the Moon shone in the sky.

raw: ततः प्रहृष्टा परिपूर्ण मानसा । यशस्विनी भर्तुर् अवेक्ष्य भाषितम् । धनानि रत्नानि च दातुम् अन्गना । प्रचक्रमे धर्मभृताम् मनस्विनी ॥२-३०-४७॥
भरत: शिरसा कृत्वा संन्यासं पादुके तत: । अब्रवीद्दु:खसन्तप्त: सर्वं प्रकृतिमण्डलम् ॥२-११५-१५॥
translation: Then Bharata placed the sandals held in trust on his head and, overcome with grief, he addressed the concourse of subjects:

raw: तपः चरन्त्या वर्षाणि दश वीर्यवताम् वर । अवशिष्टानि भद्रम् ते भ्रातरम् द्रक्ष्यसे ततः ॥१-४६-१३॥
translation: O the best of the brave ten years is yet to go (for completion of austerities). You will have a brother. May you prosper

raw: तत: प्रभाते जनक: कृतकर्मा महर्षिभि: । उवाच वाक्यं वाक्यज्ञ श्शतानन्दं पुरोहितम् ॥१-७०-१॥
translation: Thereafter at dawn after the maharshis had performed their daily (sacrificial) rites the eloquent Janaka said to the chief priest Satananda:

raw: रात्रिः शशांक उदित सौम्य वक्त्रातारा गण उन्मीलित चारु नेत्रा । ज्योत्स्ना अंशुक प्रावरणा विभातिनारी इव शुक्ल अंशुक संवृत अंगी ॥४-३०-४५॥
translation: 'The night appears like a lady with a sweet face lit up by the rising Moon, her beautiful eyes opened up by stars, her body draped in the robe of white Moon light.

raw: राजशेषा कृता लङ्का क्षीणः कोशो बलं हतम् । राजानमिममासाद्य सुहृच्चिह्नममित्रकम् ॥६-६५-७॥
translation: "The king is left alone in Lanka, which is divested of its wealth, and treasury reduced, and the army destroyed by unfriendly people pretending as good friends around him."

raw: ज्येष्ठस्य हि सुतो ज्येष्ठः सदृशो विक्रमेण च । अंगदो अयम् अदीनात्मा यौवराज्यस्य भाजनम् ॥४-२६-१३॥
translation: 'O hero consecrate Angada as heirapparent since he deserves it as the eldest son of your brother, a noble soul and equal to you in prowess.

raw: नारदस्तु महातेजा मुहूर्तं ध्यानमास्थितः । चिन्तयामास विप्रेन्द्रो विधूम इव पावकः ॥७-२०-२६॥
translation: But the greatly effulgent Narada, the chief among Brahmanas, having assumed meditation for a moment, pondered like a smokeless fire.

raw: विद्याधरैर्मुनिगणैरप्सरोभिर्निषेवितम् । नानामृगगणाकीर्णं बहुकन्दरशोभितम् ॥६-७४-४४॥
translation: From that mountain the monkey sprang to Malaya Mountain which was like Meru and Mandara mountains. It was set with various springs, covered with various trees and creepers, abounded with lotuses, frequented by Devas, Gandharvas. It was sixty yojanas high and visited by Vidhyadharas, celestial nymphs, and sages, filled with various species of deer and numerous caves. Yakshas, Gandharvas, and Kinnaras were living there. There the son of the wind god grew in size like a cloud.

raw: हरीन् च वृद्धान् उपयातु स अंगदोभवान् मम आज्ञाम् अधिकृत्य निश्चितम् । इति व्यवस्थाम् हरि पुंगव ईश्वरोविधाय वेश्म प्रविवेश वीर्यवान् ॥४-२९-३३॥
translation: 'In strict obedience to my orders, go with Angada to the elderly monkeys and inform them about my decision and order'. After making this arrangement valiant Sugriva entered his residence. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये किष्किन्धाकाण्डे एकोनत्रिंशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the twentyninth sarga of Kishkindakanda of the Holy Ramayana, the first epic, composed by sage Valmiki.

raw: बाणधारासहस्रैस्तैः स तोयद इवाम्बरात् । राघवं रावणो बाणैस्तटाकमिव पूरयत् ॥६-१०५-३॥
translation: Valiant hero, Ravana, with his eyes flaming in anger, raising his bow, rained arrows at Sri Rama. He continued to rain thousands of arrows just as rain filled the tank, his arrows covered Raghava.

raw: तथा तां क्रियमाणां च वृद्धाभिर्जन्म नाम च । सङ्कीर्तनं च रामस्य सीतायाः प्रसवौ शुभौ ॥७-६६-११॥
translation: Thus, while that (protection) was being performed by the elderly women, there was also chanting of Rama's name and glorification of Sita's two auspicious births.

raw: सा तयोः कुशलं देवी निशम्य नरसिंहयोः । प्रीतिसंहृष्टसर्वाङ्गी हनुमन्तमथाब्रवीत् ॥५-३४-५॥
translation: On hearing the wellbeing of Rama and Lakshman, lions among men, Sita experienced thrill all over her body. She then spoke to Hanuman:

raw: ततस्तौ नहशार्दूलौ दीप्यमानौ स्वतेजसा । शुक्लमाल्याम्बरधरौ जानकीं पर्युपस्थितौ ॥५-२७-१३॥
translation: "Dressed in white garlands and clothes, the two brothers, tigers among men, glowing in their effulgence approached Janaki.

raw: न च असौ रक्षसा योग्यः कूट युद्धा हि राक्षसा । विप्रयुक्तो हि रामेण मुहूर्तम् अपि न उत्सहे ॥१-२०-८॥
भवता सख्य कामौ तौ भ्रातरौ राम लक्ष्मणौ । प्रगृह्य च अर्चयस्व एतौ पूजनीयतमौ उभौ ॥४-५-७॥
translation: 'Both the brothers, Rama and Lakshmana seek friendship with you. As both of them are worthiest of worship, welcome them with due reverence.'

raw: स हि राज सुतः पुत्र चीर वासा महा वनम् । दण्डकान् सह वैदेह्या लक्ष्मण अनुचरः गतः ॥२-७२-४२॥
translation: O my son, prince Rama attired in garments of bark along with Sita and followed by Lakshmana left for the great Dandaka forest.

raw: यदिहास्य प्रियाक्ष्यातुर्न कुर्मि सदृशम् प्रियम् । एष सर्वस्वभूतस्तु परिष्वङ्गो हनुमतः ॥६-१-१३॥
समासाद्य तु तम् वृक्षम् वसेद्वातिक्रमेत वा । क्रोशमात्रम् ततो गत्वा नीलम् द्रक्ष्यथ काननम् ॥२-५५-८॥
translation: Reaching that tree, you may tarry or proceed further. A krosa from there, you will see a beautiful forest filled with dark trees mixed with Palasas and badaris and bamboos on the Yamuna.

raw: ईदृशानां सहस्राणि सायुधानां नराधम । भक्षितानि मया रोषात्कालमाकाङ्क्षसे नु किम् ॥७-६८-६॥
translation: "O vilest of men, I have devoured thousands of armed individuals like you out of anger; do you indeed desire death?"

raw: अवप्लुत्य महा वेगः प्रहस्तस्य निवेशनम् । ततो अन्यत् पुप्लुवे वेश्म महा पार्श्वस्य वीर्यवान् ॥५-६-१७॥
translation: Courageous and swift, Hanuman sprang from Prahasta's house to Mahaparshva's, and so on.

raw: नाशयत्येष वै भूतं तदेव सृजति प्रभुः । पायत्येष तपत्येष वर्षत्येष गभस्तिभिः ॥६-१०७-२२॥
translation: "Being a creator and destroyer of the world, this Sun god alone radiates, creates thirst by heat and rains to relieve.

raw: व्रजन्तं राक्षसं प्रेक्ष्य सिंहनादं प्रचुक्रुशुः । ऊचुश्चान्योन्यमाश्लिष्य सङ्क्रुद्धं प्रेक्ष्य राक्षसाः ॥६-९३-४१॥
translation: ( As Ravana marched) the Rakshasas in the abode roared like a lion seeing enraged Ravana and embraced each other (thinking of Ravana's victory) and spoke to one another.

raw: वीराः च नियतोत्साहा राज शास्त्रम् अनुष्ठिताः । शुचीनाम् रक्षितारः च नित्यम् विषय वासिनाम् ॥१-७-१२॥
translation: They were heroic. They possessed steady perseverance. They followed the state policy and always protected the virtuous people living in the state.

raw: गुणा बहु विधाः प्राप्ताः तव संदर्शनात् मया । विस्तरेण च वै ब्रह्मन् कीर्त्यमानम् महत्तपः ॥१-६५-३३॥
रसातलम् उपागच्छत् सिद्ध्यर्थम् तस्य कर्मणः । भगीरथो अपि रजार्षि गंगम् आदाय यत्नतः ॥१-४३-३९॥
नीलमेघनिभांश्चास्य सदश्वान् पर्वतोपमान् । जघानाप्लुत्य गदया रावणस्य विभीषणः ॥६-१०१-१७॥
translation: Vibheeshana struck with his formidable mace the horses of Ravana which were like dark clouds and huge like mountains.

raw: मन्गल आलम्भनीयानि प्राशनीयान् उपस्करान् । उपनिन्युस् तथा अपि अन्याः कुमारी बहुलाः स्त्रियः ॥२-६५-९॥
translation: Also, a group of women mostly young maidens brought auspicious unguents, articles gratifying the senses and those necessary accessories for completion of bathing process.

raw: स तंमहामेघनिकाशरूपमुत्पाट्यगच्छन्युधिकुम्भकर्णः । रराजमेरुप्रतिमानरूपोमेरुर्यथाभ्युछ्रचितघोरशृङ्गः ॥६-६७-७०॥
translation: In the battlefield, the form of Kumbhakarna which resembled a huge cloud was distinguished in appearance like the lofty peak of mountain Meru.

raw: अयम् एव आश्रमो राम गुणवान् रम्यताम् इति । ऋषि संघ अनुचरितः सदा मूल फलैर् युतः ॥३-७-१८॥
translation: O Rama this is a salubrious hermitage where hosts of sages live and which is full of roots and fruits, you may enjoy yourself here.

raw: माल्यवद्भुजनिर्मुक्ता शक्तिर्घण्टाकृतस्वना । हरेरुरसि बभ्राज मेघस्थेव शतह्रदा ॥७-८-१०॥
translation: The spear, released from Malyavan's arm with a bell-like sound, shone on Hari's chest like a flash of lightning in a cloud.

raw: श्रुणु तत् कर्म साहाय्ये यत् कार्यम् वचनात् मम । सौवर्णः त्वम् मृगो भूत्वा चित्रो रजत बिन्दुभिः ॥३-४०-१७॥
त्वत् विधः काम वृत्तो हि दुःशीलः पाप मंत्रितः । आत्मानम् स्व जनम् राष्ट्रम् स राजा हन्ति दुर्मतिः ॥३-३७-७॥
translation: A king who is a slave to passion, who is of bad conduct, of wicked thoughts, advised in evil ways destroys himself, his kith and kin and the entire kingdom.

raw: रामस्य उपरि संहृष्टा ववर्षुः विस्मिताः तदा । अर्थ अधिक मुहूर्तेन रामेण निशितैः शरैः ॥३-३०-३०॥
तदुक्तमतिकायस्य बलिनो बाहुशालिनः । कुम्भकर्णस्य वचनं श्रुत्वोवाच महोदरः ॥६-६४-१॥
translation: Hearing the words of mighty Kumbhakarna, of massive body and round arms Mahodara said.

raw: तत्र सत्त्व सहस्राणाम् सागर अन्तर चारिणाम् । पंथानम् एको अध्यवसम् संनिरोद्धुम् अवाङ् मुखः ॥४-५९-१३॥
translation: 'There I stood alone looking down, obstructing the path of thousands of creatures inhabiting the ocean.

raw: कुम्भकर्णस्सङ्कृद्धोगदामुद्यम्यवीर्यवान् । अर्थयन्समहाकायस्समन्ताद् व्यक्षिपद्रिपून् ॥६-६७-५॥
translation: Valiant Kumbhakarna, a gigantic one, highly enraged lifted mace and crescent shaped arrow struck the enemies on all sides.

raw: ग्रहणम् वायु सूनोश्च लंका दाह अभिगर्जनम् । प्रति प्लवनम् एव अथ मधूनाम् हरणम् तथा ॥१-३-३३॥
वज्रस्पर्शतलैर्हस्तैर्मुष्टिभिश्च हता भृशम् । वैमुः शोणितमास्येभ्यो विशीर्णदशनेक्षणाः ॥६-५८-१६॥
translation: Hit by fists and hands that had the impact of thunderbolt, teeth and eyes smashed and fallen out, the Rakshasas vomited blood from their mouth excessively.

raw: अद्यत्वयाहम्सौमित्रेबालेनापि , नापिपराक्रमैः । तोषितोगन्तुमिच्छामित्यामनुज्ञाप्यराघवम् ॥६-६७-११०॥
translation: "Now I am gratified with your valour, though young. Taking leave of you, I wish to go to Raghava."

raw: नर्मदापुलिने हृद्ये शुभ्राभ्रसदृशप्रभे । राक्षसैस्तु मुहूर्तेन कृतः पुष्पमयो गिरिः ॥७-३१-३७॥
translation: On the charming sandbank of the Narmada, which shone like a white cloud, the Rākṣasas swiftly created a mountain of flowers in a moment.

raw: न शक्यम् खल्वियम् लङ्का प्रवेष्टुम् वानर त्वया । रक्षिता रावणबलैरभिगुप्ता समन्ततः ॥५-३-२४॥
translation: "O vanara this Lanka is a secret place protected by Ravana's army everywhere. It is surely not possible for you to enter this city".

raw: कामरूपधराः शूराः सुभीमा भीमदर्शनाः । राक्षसा वा सहस्राणि राक्षसाधिप निश्चिताः ॥६-८-१३॥
translation: "O Lord of Rakshasas Thousands of fearful Rakshasas capable of assuming any form at free will, heroic ones of frightful appearance should tell Rama the foremost of Raghus, quietly going near him in human form."

raw: पाण्डुरारुणवर्णानि स्रोओताम्सि विमलान्यपि । सुस्रुवुर्गिरिधातुभ्यः सभस्मानि भुजङ्गवत् ॥२-६३-१९॥
translation: Although pure, the rapidly flowing water from the mountains mixed with the minerals in the soil turned white and red in colour and flowed like a serpent.

raw: पुष्पाणि च सुगन्धीनि क्रियतां तेषु नित्यशः । परिवार्य यथा मे स्युरध्यर्धं योजनं तथा ॥७-५४-१२॥
translation: Let fragrant flowers always be placed in them, surrounding the area for me to a distance of one and a half Yojanas.

raw: अनुक्तः अपि अत्रभवता भवत्या वचनात् अहम् । वने वत्स्यामि विजने वर्षाणि इह चतुर् दश ॥२-१९-२३॥
translation: Though this has not been said by my respectable father himself, I shall live in the forlorn forest for fourteen years in accordance with your word.

raw: सा क्षिप्ता राक्षसेन्द्रस्य तस्मिन् शूले पपात ह । भिन्नः शक्त्या महान् शूलो निपपात हतद्युतिः ॥६-१०४-२८॥
translation: With the hurling of the javelin by Rama at the great trident of Ravana and on (the javelin) touching the trident, it was broken, lost its splendour and fell down.

raw: धनेश्वरस्त्वथ पितृवाक्यगौरवान्न्यवेशयच्छशिविमले गिरौ पुरीम् । स्वलङ्कृतैर्भवनवरैर्विभूषितां पुरन्दरस्वेव तदा ऽमरावतीम् ॥७-११-५२॥
translation: But then Kubera, out of respect for his father's words, established a city on the moon-bright mountain (Kailasa), adorned with well-decorated excellent mansions, just like Indra's Amaravati. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकादशः सर्गः ।। 11 ।। Thus ends the eleventh sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

raw: कवचं ब्रह्मदत्तं मे यदादित्यसमप्रभम् । देवासुरविमर्देषु न भिन्नं वज्रशक्तिभिः ॥६-९३-३०॥
translation: 'I was given a shield by Brahma, effulgent like the Sun which the Devas or Danavas could not break with their thunderbolt fists'.

raw: अचिरेण एव कालेन परिवाहान् बहु उदकान् । चक्रुर् बहु विध आकारान् सागर प्रतिमान् बहून् ॥२-८०-११॥
translation: In a short time they constructed many water reservoirs of different shapes capable of holding large volumes of water like the sea.

raw: मनोरथो अयम् इष्टो अस्या भगिन्या मम राक्षसाः । शीघ्रम् संपद्यताम् गत्वा तौ प्रमथ्य स्व तेजसा ॥३-१९-२४॥
translation: O demons quickly go and crush them with your power and fulfil my sister's sincere wish.

raw: दिलीपेन महाभाग तव पित्रा अतितेजसा । पुनर् न शकिता नेतुम् गंगाम् प्रार्थयत अनघ ॥१-४४-११॥
translation: O Sinless one (Bhagiratha) O Distinguished one on the part of Dilipa brilliant your father who had the virtuous of a rajarshi, who was equal to a maharshi in splendour, and to me in austerities and abiding to the duties of a kshatriya it was even not possible to bring Ganga through prayer.

raw: इमानि च फलान्यत्र स्वादूनि विविधानि च । जातानि पर्वताग्रेषु चास्वाद्यास्वाद्य गायताम् ॥७-९३-८॥
translation: While singing, they should repeatedly taste these various delicious fruits that grow on the mountain peaks.

raw: ग्रसन्तमिव चाकाशं नादयन्तं वसुन्धराम् । प्रणाशं परसैन्यानां स्वसैन्यानां प्रहर्षणम् । रावणस्य रथं क्षिप्रं चोदयामास सारथिः ॥६-१०८-३॥
translation: Delighted charioteer drove the chariot of Ravana with speed. It was of the shape of the abode of Gandharvas, capable of destroying enemy's army. It had rows of excellent flags, richly endowed, like the best piece of artwork. It was fixed with flag posts in rows touching the sky and filling space. It was yoked to excellent horses adorned with gold chains and equipped with implements for war. The earth was resounding as it was driven as if to crush the enemy's army and its own army was happy.

raw: सुरथेनाग्निवर्णेन कामगेन महारथः । अभिदुद्राव सेनां तां वनान्यग्निरिव ज्वलन् ॥७-२८-३॥
translation: The great charioteer, Meghanada, with his beautiful, fiery-colored chariot that moved at will, rushed towards that army, burning like a fire consuming forests.

raw: तत्रस्थः स तदा गन्धम् पान भक्ष्य अन्न सम्भवम् । दिव्यम् सम्मूर्चितम् जिघ्रन् रूपवन्तम् इव अनिलम् ॥५-९-२०॥
translation: There he smelt the stupefying, unearthly odour of food and drink. He felt as though the fragrance had taken a potentially solid form. (Note: The wind has no form. But when he carried the aroma of food and drink it appeared like the personification of wind which could be smelt. गन्धवती पृथवी fragrance comes from earth पृथवीतत्त्व the poet transmits the same to the wind who has got only स्पर्श sense of touch).

raw: सा तस्य धर्मार्थ समाधि युक्तम्निशम्य वाक्यम् मधुर स्वभावम् । तारा गतार्थे मनुजेन्द्र कार्येविश्वास युक्तम् तम् उवाच भूयः ॥४-३३-५०॥
translation: Tara heard the sweet words of Lakshmana which showed his good understanding of dharma and artha. What she said to him in reply reflects her faith in Sugriva's effort to help Rama's cause:

raw: पक्षवन्तः पुरा पुत्र बभूवुः पर्वतोत्तमाः । छन्दतः पृथिवीं चेरुर्बाधमानाः समन्ततः ॥५-५८-१४॥
translation: 'O son in the past, foremost of the mountains too had wings and they used to range at will all over the earth tormenting all.

raw: अवस्थितं हनूमन्तं ते दृष्ट्वा हरियूथपाः । बभूवुर्बलवन्तो हि बलवन्तं समाश्रिताः ॥६-५६-१०॥
translation: Seeing Hanuman, the monkey leaders took their shelter under him, got established firmly and became strong.

raw: ततः सोम आश्रमम् गत्वा देव गन्धर्व सेवितम् । कालम् नाम महासानुम् पर्वतम् तम् गमिष्यथ ॥४-४३-१४॥
translation: 'Then go and explore the hermitage of Soma inhabited by gods and gandharvas and also the great summits of mount Kala.

raw: आत्मनः सदृशं वीरः स तं निक्षिप्य वानरम् । सुग्रीवो ऽभिमुखः शत्रुं प्रतस्थे पादपायुधः ॥६-९७-७॥
translation: Sugriva, being a hero himself, uprooting a tree as a weapon, went towards the enemy after having assigned Sushena the responsibility of protection of Vanaras.

raw: बहून्मेध्यान् मृगान् हत्वा चेरतुर्यमुनावने । विहृत्य ते बर्हिणपूगनादिते । शुभे वने वानरवारणायुते । समम् नदीवप्रमुपेत्य सम्मतम् । निवासमाजग्मु रदीनदर्शनाः ॥२-५५-३४॥
translation: They reached the tableland on the bank of that river and moved in high spirit in the lovely forest resounding with cries of flocks of peacocks and teeming with monkeys and elephants. Finally they selected a spot for their stay. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे पञ्चपञ्चाशस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the fiftyfifth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

raw: कर्दमेनैवमुक्तास्तु सर्व एव द्विजर्षभाः । रोचयन्ति स्म तं यज्ञं रुद्रस्याराधनं प्रति ॥७-९०-१३॥
translation: All the eminent Brahmins, thus addressed by Kardama, approved of that sacrifice intended for the worship of Rudra.

raw: स तु स्रेष्ठैर्गुणैर्युक्तः प्रजानां पार्थिवात्मजः । बहिश्चर इव प्राणो बभूव गुणतः प्रियः ॥२-१-१९॥
translation: Bestowed with such excellent qualities, the prince (Rama) became a favourite of his subjects. He was like their vital life outside their bodies.

raw: ततः संसक्तहस्तस्तु रावणो लोकरावणः । नाराचमालां रामस्य ललाटे प्रत्यमुञ्चत ॥६-१००-३४॥
translation: Then Ravana, who made the people cry, whose hands were engaged in the fight, discharged a row of steel arrows into Rama's forehead.

raw: इमास्तु खलु राक्षस्यो यदि त्वमनुमन्यसे । हन्तुमिच्छाम्यहं सर्वा याभिस्त्वं तर्जिता पुरा ॥६-११६-३१॥
translation: "I desire to kill all those Rakshasas who in the past have intimidated you indeed and whoever threatened you."

raw: तापसाश्रमवासिन्याः प्राज्यमूलफलोदके । तस्मिन् सिद्धाश्रमे देशे मन्दाकिन्या ह्यदूरतः ॥५-३८-१३॥
translation: 'Long ago we were staying at Siddhasrama. This hermitage was situated to the northeast at the foot of Chitrakuta mountain which was not far from the river Mandakini. It had abundant roots, fruits and water. You sported with me in the gardens which were fragrant with many types of flowers and ponds. You sat down on my lap with wet clothes in the hermitage'.

raw: तपः चचार काकुत्स्थ परमम् परम आत्मवान् । एतस्मिन् एव काले तु सत्य वादी जित इन्द्रियः ॥१-५८-१०॥
वाताश्च कलुषा वान्ति कम्पते च वसुन्धरा । पर्वताग्राणि वेपन्ते पतन्ति च महीरुःआः ॥६-२३-४॥
translation: "The wind is blowing mixed with dust, even the earth is cracking, mountain tops are shaking, and huge trees are breaking and falling down."

raw: सङ्क्रुद्धस्त्वं हि धर्मात्मन् गत्वा तस्याश्रमं मुनेः । दृष्टवांश्च तदा तां स्त्रीं दीप्तामग्निशिखामिव ॥७-३०-३०॥
translation: Indeed, you, being very angry, O righteous one, went to that sage's hermitage and then saw that woman shining like a flame of fire.

raw: भीमनासापुटं तं तु पातालविपुलाननम् । शय्यायां न्यस्तसर्वाङ्गं मेदोरुधिरगन्धिनम् ॥६-६०-२९॥
इति इव तम् शोक विधेय देहम्रामम् विसंज्ञम् विलपंतम् एव । उवाच सौमित्रिःअदीन सत्त्वःन्याये स्थितः काल युतम् च वाक्यम् ॥३-६३-१८॥
translation: While Rama was thus in tears, in a state of sorrow and swoon, Lakshmana who was rational and courageous spoke to him words appropriate to the time :

raw: पुष्पितान् पुष्पित अग्राभिर् लताभिर् उपशोभितान् । ददर्श रामः शतशः तत्र कान्तार पादपान् ॥३-११-७५॥
वरदानकृतैश्वर्यं सा तं प्राप्य पतिं प्रियम् । आसीद्देववती तुष्टा धनं प्राप्येव निर्धनः ॥७-५-३॥
translation: Having obtained him, her dear husband whose prosperity was due to boons, Devavati became as pleased as a poor man who has acquired wealth.

raw: लक्ष्मणेन तु तद्वाक्यमुक्तं श्रुत्वा स राघवः । सन्दधे परवीरघ्नो धनुरादाय वीर्यवान् । रावणाय शरान् घोरान् विससर्ज चमूमुखे ॥६-१०३-१॥
translation: Courageous Raghava, the destroyer of enemies on hearing the words spoken by Lakshmana took up his bow and fixed it.

raw: ब्रूयाः च हि महा राजम् भरतम् क्षिप्रम् आनय । आगतः च अपि भरतः स्थाप्यो नृप मते पदे ॥२-५२-३२॥
translation: Tell the king to send for Bharata quickly, and on his arrival, he be placed in the position of the king as per his own desire.

raw: अवकीर्णस्ततस्ताभिर्हनुमाञ्छरवृष्टिभिः । अभवत् संवृताकारः शैलराडिव वृष्टिभिः ॥५-४५-८॥
translation: Later, Hanuman covered with showers of arrows scattered all over appeared like the king of mountains shot with showers of rain.

raw: तत् गतम् हृदयम् हि अस्याः तत् अधीनम् च जीवितम् । अयोध्या अपि भवेत् तस्या राम हीना तथा वनम् ॥२-६०-११॥
translation: Her heart is ever united with Rama, and her life is under his control. Without Rama, even Ayodhya would become a forest for her.

raw: स तु नालीकनाराचैर्गदाभिर्मुसलैरपि । रक्षोभिः संवृतः सङ्ख्ये वानरान् विचकर्त ह ॥६-७३-३०॥
translation: Indrajith, remaining concealed and surrounded by Rakshasas, destroyed the Vanaras with nalikas, steel arrows and maces.

raw: विज्ञाप्यश्च नरव्याघ्रो रामो वायुसुत त्वया । अखिलेनेह यद् दृष्टमिति मामाह जानकी ॥५-६५-२०॥
translation: (She said)'O son of the Windgod you should let Rama, the tiger among men know all that you have seen here.

raw: न ह्येकः साधको हेतुः स्वल्पस्यापीह कर्मणः । यो ह्यर्थं बहुधा वेद स समर्थो ऽर्थसाधने ॥५-४१-६॥
translation: 'There are ways more than one even to perform a small work. And the capable know it.

raw: सुसुखे हि बहु द्रव्ये तस्मिन् हि धरणी धरे । वसतः तस्य रामस्य रतिः अल्पा अपि न अभवत् ॥४-२७-३०॥
translation: Though Rama was residing in comfort on the mountain richly endowed with many pleasant things, he experienced little happiness.

raw: हित बुद्ध्या खलु वचो मया एतत् अभिधीयते । सदा सुखम् न जानामि दुह्खम् एव सदा वनम् ॥२-२८-६॥
translation: I am saying all this in your interest. The forest is a haven of hardships. I know of no happiness in the forest.

raw: राक्षसीनां वचः श्रुत्वा रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः । हुताग्निरिव जज्वाल कोपसंवर्तितेक्षणः ॥५-४२-२२॥
translation: On listening to the report of the ogresses, Ravana, the lord of demons flared up like blazing flame of a sacrificial fire, his eyeballs rolling in rage.

raw: ततः तु सा राक्षस संघ सम्वृतम् खरम् जन स्थान गतम् विरूपिता । उपेत्य तम् भ्रातरम् उग्र तेजसम् पपात भूमौ गगनाद् यथा अशनिः ॥३-१८-२५॥
translation: A disfigured demoness, she fell down like the thunderbolt from the sky on the ground while her fiercelooking brother Khara sat surrounded by demons at Janasthana.

raw: तेषामापततां शीघ्रं निघ्नतां चापि वानरान् । द्विविदो गिरिशृङ्गेण जघानैकं नरान्तकम् ॥६-५८-२०॥
translation: Rushing at great speed, the Rakshasas and also killing the Vanaras in that way, Dwivida alone struck down Naranthaka with a mountain peak.

raw: अधर्मसंश्रितो धर्मो विनाशयति राघव । सर्वमेतद्यथाकामं काकुत्स्थ कुरुते नरः ॥६-८३-३०॥
translation: "Kakuthsa Rama! Kings followed dharma and adharma both according to context. Whether following dharma or adharma destruction is happening. Therefore, humans keep doing both as per their desire."

raw: उपन्यस्तमपन्यस्तं युद्धमार्गविशारदौ । तौ विचेरतुर्न्योन्यं वानरेन्द्रश्च रावणः ॥६-४०-२६॥
translation: Both Vanara king and Ravana being learned in war craft, went around in circles like ox's urine, stood in different wonderful postures, moved forward and backward horizontally and obliquely to evade movements, hitting, and delivering each other, standing steadily motionless, striking, jumping, assaulting each other coming forward and going away, going backwards jumping from behind, holding hands and folding to resist exhibiting their skill in combat.

raw: स राजा तेन वाक्येन प्रत्याश्वस्तो महामतिः । प्रत्युवाच ततो वाक्यं दीनो भृत्यक्षयाद् भृशम् ॥७-८९-१५॥
translation: That great-minded king, though reassured by those words, then replied with great distress due to the loss of his servants.

raw: ततः कैलासकूटाभं चतुर्दन्तं मदस्रवम् । शृङ्गारधारिणं प्रांशुं स्वर्णघण्टाट्टहासिनम् ॥७-३५-३७॥
translation: Then (Indra's elephant) appeared, resembling the peak of Kailasa, four-tusked, with ichor flowing, adorned with ornaments, tall, and making a loud sound with its golden bells.

raw: इति पादातयोधाश्च हस्त्यश्वारोह बन्धका: । अनाथास्तं विधिं लब्ध्वा वाचमेतामुदैरयन् ॥२-९१-५९॥
translation: Having enjoyed the hospitality of Bharadwaja the foot soldiers, horse and elephant riders made utterances ignoring their leaders.

raw: मम लालस्य मानस्य सुतार्थम् नास्ति वै सुखम् । तदर्थम् हयमेधेन यक्ष्ह्यामि इति मतिर् मम ॥१-८-८॥
translation: There is no happiness for one who has no son. This is the cause of my intense suffering. Therefore, I have made up my mind to perform a horsesacrifice.

raw: इति एवम् आर्तस्य रघु प्रवीरः श्रुत्वा वचो वालि जघन्य जस्य । संजात बाष्प पर वीर हन्ता रामो मुहूर्तम् विमना बभूव ॥४-२४-२४॥
translation: Rama, the hero of the Raghu dynasty, a destroyer of the enemy heroes, was moved to tears. He lost composure for a moment when he heard Sugriva's lament.

raw: बुद्ध्यस्व सृपशार्दूल कुरु कार्यमनन्तरम् । उदतिष्ठत रामस्य समग्रमभिषेचन्म् ॥२-१४-५४॥
translation: O best among kings the holy night has passed. Having been acquainted with the acts accomplished so far, perform whatever is further necessary for the installation ceremony. All preparations for Rama's coronation ceremony have since been complete.

raw: ततः क्रुद्धो महाबाहुर्धनुश्चिच्छेद रक्षसः । अष्टाभिरथ नाराचैः सूतं विव्याध राघवः ॥६-७९-२९॥
translation: Then broad shouldered Raghava was enraged and split the bow with eight steel arrows and the charioteer also.

raw: सो ऽभिनिर्याय नगरादिन्द्रजित् समितिञ्जयः । हुत्वा ऽग्निं राक्षसैर्मन्त्रैरन्तर्धानगतो ऽब्रवीत् ॥६-८०-१६॥
translation: Indrajith who had acquired the power of being victorious in the wars departed, after uttering ritualistic verses which are known to Rakshasas only and making an offering into fire disappeared and bragged as follows.

raw: नाना आकाराणि वासांसि फलन्ति अन्ये नगोत्तमाः । मुक्ता वैदूर्य चित्राणि भूषणानि तथैव च । स्त्रीणाम् यानि अनुरूपाणि पुरुषाणाम् तथैव च ॥४-४३-४५॥
सौमित्रिं सा विनिर्भिद्य प्रविष्टा धरणीतलम् ॥६-१०१-४३॥
ऊचुश्च ते महात्मानो हर्षेण महता वृताः । उपपन्नं नरश्रेष्ठ तवैव भुवि नान्यतः ॥७-६०-१६॥
translation: And those great souls, filled with great joy, said, "O best among men, such a statement is fitting only for you on earth, and for no one else."

raw: अयोध्या अधिपते वीर शापात् चण्डालताम् गतः । अथ तत् वाक्यम् आकर्ण्य राजा चण्डालताम् गतः ॥१-५७-१६॥
कपिशोणितदिग्धाङ्गंभक्ष्यन्तंप्लवङ्गमान् । कुम्भकर्णंस्थितंदृष्टवासुग्रीवोवाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥६-६७-५५॥
translation: Sugriva spoke these words seeing Kumbhakarna who stood smeared with the blood of Vanaras and eating monkeys.

raw: तौ दृष्ट्वा भ्रातरौ तत्र वीरौ सा पुरुषर्षभौ । शयानौ पुण्डरीकाक्षौ कुमाराविव पावकी ॥६-४७-२०॥
ततो नील अम्बुद निभः प्रहस्तो नाम राक्षसः । अब्रवीत् प्राञ्जलिर् वाक्यम् शूरः सेना पतिस्तदा ॥६-८-१॥
translation: Then a Rakshasa whose body was like a dark cloud, called Prahastha, the heroic chief of the army, spoke these words with folded palms.

raw: ततो अब्रवीत् सुसम्क्रुद्धो वज्र दम्ष्ट्रो महाबलः । प्रगृह्य परिघम् घोरम् माम्स शोणित रूपितम् ॥६-८-९॥
translation: Then a mighty strong one who was endowed with diamond like teeth highly enraged, clasping a dreadful iron bludgeon stained with flesh and blood spoke.

raw: ददृज़ुह् ज़िखरे तस्य विषक्ताम् इव खे पुरीम् । ताम् ज़ुभाम् प्रवत द्वाराम् प्राकार वर ज़ोभिताम् ॥६-३८-१५॥
एवम् उक्त्वा धनुष् पाणिः क्रोध विस्फारित ईक्षणः । बभूव रामो दुर्धर्षो युग अन्त अग्निर् इव ज्वलन् ॥६-२१-२५॥
translation: Having spoken like that, Rama with his flaming red eyes seemed like the flame at the end of the universe and unassailable.

raw: एषा प्रसन्न सलिला पद्म नील उत्पलायुता । हंस कारण्डव आकीर्णा पम्पा सौगन्धिका युता ॥४-१-६३॥
translation: 'This Pampa with its water clear and fragrant with red and blue lotuses is filled with swans and geese.

raw: यदि त्वम् यास्यसि वनम् त्यक्त्वा माम् शोक लालसाम् । अहम् प्रायम् इह आसिष्ये न हि शक्ष्यामि जीवितुम् ॥२-२१-२६॥
translation: If you depart for the forest leaving me griefstricken I cannot live. Here I shall seek death by fasting.

raw: काले वर्षति पर्जन्यः पातयन्नमृतं पयः । वाताश्चापि प्रवान्त्येते स्पर्शयुक्ताः सुखाः शिवाः ॥७-४१-२०॥
translation: The clouds rain nectar-like water at the proper time, and these winds blow, pleasant to the touch, agreeable, and auspicious.

raw: भूषणानि च मुख्यानि दृष्टानि धरणी तले । अनया एव अपविद्धानि स्वनवन्ति महान्ति च ॥५-१५-४६॥
translation: "The jingling, choice ornaments were thrown down on the ground.

raw: तत्र आसीत् पिन्गलो गार्ग्यः त्रिजटः नाम वै द्विजः । क्षतवृत्तिर्वने नित्यम् फालकुद्दाललाङ्गली ॥२-३२-२९॥
translation: A brahmin by name, Trijata, a descendant of sage Garga and of reddishbrown colour used to live in that region earning his livelihood in the forest by digging the earth with an ironspade and a plough.

raw: मया एकन तु निर्युक्तः परिमुच्यस्व राघव । माम् हि भूत बलिम् दत्त्वा पलास्व यथा सुखम् ॥३-६९-३९॥
इष्ट्याम् तु वर्तमानायाम् कुशनाभम् महीपतिम् । उवाच परमोदारः कुशो ब्रह्मसुतः तदा ॥१-३४-२॥
translation: Then, while putreshti was on Kusa the highly generous son of Brahma, said to king Kusanabha :

raw: उपायं नाधिगच्छामो यथा नदनदीपतिम् । तराम तरसा सर्वे ससैन्या वरुणालयम् । एवमुक्तस्तु धर्मज्ञः प्रत्युवाच विभीषणः ॥६-१९-३१॥
translation: "What strategy should we adopt to cross this abode of Varuna, the Lord of rivers and streams with the entire army of Vanaras?" (Hanuman and Sugriva asked Vibheeshana).

raw: स ब्रह्मणा दत्तवरस्त्रैलोक्यं बाधते भृशम् । भवतामर्थसिद्ध्यर्थं कालेन स समागतः । अद्यैव क्षमितव्यं मे भवन्तो विगतज्वराः ॥६-४४-३६॥
पुत्रं तं वारयित्वा तु स्वयमेव व्यवस्थितः । सो ऽपि युद्धाद्विनिष्क्रम्य रावणिः समुपाविशत् ॥७-२८-३२॥
translation: Having restrained his son, he himself took his position, while Ravani, having exited the battle, also sat down.

raw: रामागमनमाकाङ्क्षन् भरतो भ्रातृवत्सल: । भ्रातुर्वचनकारी च प्रतिज्ञापारगस्तथा ॥२-११५-२४॥
translation: Bharata who was attached to his brother and ever obedient to him, fulfilled his vow. He coronated the sandals and lived at Nandigrama longing for the return of Rama.

raw: प्रीतो हृष्टमना वाक्यमब्रवीत्पर्वतः कपिम् । मानुषं धारयन् रूपमात्मनः शिखरे स्थितः ॥५-१-१११॥
translation: Now the mountain assumed a human form and standing on its own summit, which stood very high, and glad at heart, addressed the heroic vanara gone to the aerial region.

raw: हतमिन्द्रजितं दृष्ट्वा शयानं समरक्षितौ । राक्षसानां सहस्रेषु न कश्चित् प्रत्यदृश्यत ॥६-९१-८३॥
translation: Indrajith was lying, having fallen on the ground, and not even one of the thousands of Rakshasas was present there to see.

raw: यत्तु शक्यं वयस्येन सुहृदा च परन्तप । कृतं सुग्रीव तत्सर्वं भवता धर्मभीरुणा ॥६-४९-२९॥
translation: "Sugriva! It is not possible for human beings to overcome God (destiny). O scorcher of enemies! Sugriva, my best friend, you have all done righteously that which is not possible."

raw: ततोऽब्रवीन्महाबाहुर्लकमणम् लक्ष्मणाग्रजः । सम्निवेद्य यथान्याय मात्मानमृष्ये प्रभुः ॥२-५६-१८॥
translation: The mightyarmed elder brother of Lakshmana revealed his identity to the sage by duly introducing himself. And said then to Lakshmana:

raw: विचित्य दक्षिणामाशामागतैर्हरिपुङ्गवैः ॥५-६३-१५॥
translation: 'O venerable Lakshmana Dadhimukha as complaining that the fruits and honey have been consumed by the vanara heroes, Angada and others who have come after their search for Sita in the southern direction.

raw: कच्चित् सहस्रान् मूर्खाणामेकमिच्छसि पण्डितम् । पण्डितो ह्यर्थकृच्छ्रेषु कुर्य्यान्नि:श्रेयसं महत् ॥२-१००-२३॥
translation: I hope by setting aside a thousand fools, you prefer a single wise man. A wise man will be of immense help in difficult situations.

raw: अहितं च हिताकारं धार्ष्ट्याज्जल्पन्ति ये नराः । अवेक्ष्य मन्त्रबाह्यास्ते कर्तव्याः कृत्यदूषणाः ॥६-६३-१६॥
translation: "Those who tender advice, which is unwholesome but in wholesome grab, out of their impudence should be kept away from discussion examining early as they mar the purpose."

raw: ततो नित्यानुगस्तेषां विदितात्मा महामति: । मृदुर्दान्तश्च शान्तश्च रामे च दृढभक्तिमान् ॥२-१०२-२२॥
धिङ्मामनार्यामसतीं याहं तेन विना कृता । मुहूर्तमपि रक्षामि जीवितं पापजीविता ॥५-२४-६॥
विषाणयोर्गृहीत्वा तं दुन्दुभिं गिरिसन्निभम् । आविध्यत तदा वाली विनदन्कपिकुञ्जरः ॥४-११-४०॥
translation: 'Vali, the elephantlike monkey then held the mountainlike Dundubhi by the horns and struck him down, roaring loudly.

raw: दैवम् च मानुषम् च एव कर्म ते साधु अनुष्टितम् । वसिष्ठम् च समागम्य कुशलम् मुनिपुंगवः ॥१-१८-४७॥
तम् प्रेक्ष्य रामः सुभृशम् अवध्यम् अचल उपमम् । भयेषु अभय दः श्रीमान् इदम् वचनम् अब्रवीत् ॥३-४-९॥
translation: Seeing the mountainlike Viradha not dying though seriously wounded, illustrious Rama, guaranter of safety from fear said to Lakshmana:

raw: तमास्थाय रथश्रेष्ठो महामेघसमस्वनम् । प्रययौ रक्षसाम् श्रेष्ठो दशग्रीवः सभाम् प्रति ॥६-११-४॥
translation: The tenheaded Ravana, eminent one among Rakshasas climbed up that best of chariots that was making noise like the roaring sound of a huge cloud and went to assembly.

raw: अङ्गदे समनुप्राप्ते सुग्रीवो वानराधिपः । उवाच शोकोपहतं रामं कमललोचनम् ॥५-६४-२४॥
translation: Seeing the griefstricken, lotuseyed Rama, the lord of the vanaras Sugriva said this before the arrival of Angada:

raw: समाप्तकर्मा हि स राक्षसाधिपो भवत्यदृस्यः समरे सुरासुरैः । युयुत्सता तेन समाप्तकर्मणा भवेत् सुराणामपि संशयो महान् ॥६-८४-२२॥
क्षयं नीता महाराज सपर्वतसरिद्द्रुमा । एते चान्ये च बहवो बलवन्तो दुरासदाः ॥७-२२-२७॥
translation: O great king, these and many other powerful and formidable beings, along with mountains, rivers, and trees, were all brought to destruction.

raw: कच्चिन् न ब्राह्मण वधम् हृतम् रामेण कस्यचित् । कच्चिन् न आढ्यो दरिद्रः वा तेन अपापो विहिम्सितः ॥२-७२-४४॥
translation: I hope Rama did not seize the wealth of any brahmin nor did any harm to an innocent person, whether rich or poor.

raw: स तस्य पततः खड्गं समाच्छिद्य महाकपिः । ननाद गिरिसङ्काशस्त्रासयन् सर्वनैर्ऋतान् ॥६-७०-४४॥
translation: Taking the sword from Trisira, as he was falling, the great Vanara who resembled a mountain roared, creating terror in all, surrounded there.

raw: एवं चेद्धर्मवृद्धिश्च नृणां चायुर्विवर्धनम् । भविष्यति नरश्रेष्ठ बालस्यास्य च जीवितम् ॥७-७४-३३॥
translation: O best of men, if this is done, there will be an increase in righteousness and the lifespan of men, and this child's life will also be restored. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे चतुःसप्ततितमः सर्गः ।। 74 ।। Thus ends the seventy-fourth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

raw: उपोपविष्टस्तु तथा स वीर्यवांस्तपस्विवेषेण समीक्ष्य राघवम् । श्रिया ज्वलन्तं भरत: कृताञ्जलिर्यथा महेन्द्र: प्रयत: प्रजापतिम् ॥२-१०३-३०॥
translation: Beholding Rama attired like an ascetic but radiant with a majestic glow, the extremely valiant Bharata sat near him with folded palms like the great Indra purified by religious austerities sits near Brahma, the creator.

raw: ततो वयमितस्तुर्णम् शूलशक्तिगदाधराः । चापबाणासिहस्तश्च त्वरितास्तत्र यामहे ॥६-८-१६॥
translation: "Then from here we will go there wielding tridents, javelins, maces, swords and arrows."

raw: गृह्य शाखाः प्रशाखाश्च स्कन्धांश्चोत्तमशाखिनाम् । दृष्ट्वा विपरिधावन्तं भवेयुर्भयशङ्किताः ॥५-३०-२४॥
translation: "Seeing me holding big and small branches of large trees and leaping from one place to the other, the ogresses will get scared.

raw: तस्मिन् हते भीमपराक्रमेण प्लवङ्गमानामृषभेण युद्धे । मही सशैला सवना चचाल भयं च रक्षांस्यधिकं विवेश ॥६-७६-९३॥
तदप्यशनिसङ्काशैश्छिन्नं रामेण सायकैः । एवमेकशतं छिन्नं शिरसां तुल्यवर्चसाम् ॥६-११०-२९॥
translation: Rama cut off the afore said head with Indra's thunderbolt like arrows. In that way equally charming a hundred heads were struck off.

raw: अस्मिन् क्षणे महाबाहो रावणं त्वं वधिष्यसि । एवमुक्त्वा तदा ऽगस्त्यो जगाम च यथागतम् ॥६-१०७-२७॥
translation: Agastya having spoken in that way to the mighty armed Rama to worship the Sun God and assuring him that the very moment he will be able to kill Ravana, left in the same way.

raw: यां कपीनां सहस्राणि सुबहून्ययुतानि च । दिक्षु सर्वासु मार्गन्ते सेयमासादिता मया ॥५-३०-३॥
translation: "This is Sita whom thousands of vanaras are searching in all directions.

raw: नैव साम्ना न दानेन न भेदेन कुतो युधा । सा द्रुष्टुमपि शक्येत नैव चान्येन केनचित् ॥६-८४-१२॥
तं समीक्ष्य महासत्त्वं सत्त्ववान् हरिसत्तमः । वाक्यमर्थवदव्यग्रस्तमुवाच दशाननम् ॥५-५१-१॥
translation: Hanuman, the best of monkeys, looking at the very powerful Ravana spoke slowly these highly meaningful words.

raw: स याच्यमानः काकुत्स्थः स्वाभिः प्रकृतिभिस् तदा । कुर्वाणः पितरम् सत्यम् वनम् एव अन्वपद्यत ॥२-४५-४॥
translation: Although entreated by his subjects (not to go) Rama proceeded to the forest to make his father's vow come true.

raw: कैकेय्याः प्रिय कामार्थम् तम् रामम् न अभिषेचयत् । अभिषेकाय तु पितुः समीपम् रामम् आगतम् ॥३-४७-१३॥
रथोद्वहनखिन्नाश्च त इमे रथवाजिनः । दीना धर्मपरिश्रान्ता गावो वर्षहता इव ॥६-१०६-१६॥
translation: "The horses of my chariot were exhausted by dragging, broken down, worn out by the hot sun, and desperate like cows lashed by rain."

raw: अनन्य भावाम् अनुरक्त चेतसम् । त्वया वियुक्ताम् मरणाय निश्चिताम् । नयस्व माम् साधु कुरुष्व याचनाम् । न ते मया अतः गुरुता भविष्यति ॥२-२७-२२॥
translation: Since I have no thought other than you and my heart is (irretrievably) attached to you I have resolved to die if separated from you. Pray, be favourably disposed to take me. I shall not be a burden to you.

raw: एवम् ब्रुवाणौ काकुत्स्थौ त्वरमाणौ युयुत्सया । सर्वे ते मुनयः प्रीताः प्रशशंसुर् नृपात्मजौ ॥१-३०-३॥
translation: The sages (of the asrama) were very pleased. They extolled the princes of Kakustha dynasty, who were eager to fight the rakshasas.

raw: चतुर्दश सहस्राणि रक्षसाम् भीम कर्मणाम् । एकः च रामो धर्मात्मा कथम् युद्धम् भविष्यति ॥३-२४-२२॥
translation: Thus looking at one another they discussed among themselves how there can be war between the righteous Rama fighting singlehanded on the one hand and the fourteen thousand demons, performers of terrific deeds, on the other.

raw: उपरुध्यन्ति मे प्राणा दृष्टिर् भ्रमति राघव । पश्यामि वृक्षान् सौवर्णान् उशीर कृत मूर्धजान् ॥३-६८-११॥
translation: O scion of the Raghu race, I am gasping for breath. My eyes are reeling. I see root hair growing on the tops of golden trees.

raw: स्मरंतः पुत्र दाराणाम् नित्य उद्विग्ना बुभुक्षिताः । खेदिता दुःख शय्याभिः त्वाम् करिष्यन्ति पृष्ठतः ॥४-५४-१७॥
translation: 'The memory of their sons and wives will haunt these hungry monkeys. The inconvenient bed will make them so depressed that they will leave you behind.

raw: तदप्रियं दीनमुखा रावणस्य निशाचराः । कृत्स्नं निवेदयामासुर्यथावद्वाक्यकोविदाः ॥६-५१-१०॥
translation: Rakshasas who were well versed in talking, desperately conveyed the unpleasantness as it is to Ravana.

raw: पुरस्तादृषभो वीरो नील: कुमुद एव च । पन्थानं शोधयन्तिस्म वानरैर्बहुभि स्सह ॥६-४-३०॥
translation: Heroic Rshaba, Nila and even Kumuda together with many vanaras were searching on the way.

raw: हंसानां हि पुरा राम नीलवर्णः सपाण्डुरः । पक्षा नीलाग्रसंवीताः क्रोडाः शष्पाग्रनिर्मलाः ॥७-१८-३३॥
translation: Indeed, O Rama, in the past, swans were blue-colored with a whitish tinge, their wings were covered with blue tips, and their breasts were pure like the tips of fresh grass.

raw: एवम् एतत् विचेतव्यम् भवद्भिः वानरोत्तमैः । तत् उग्र शासनम् भर्तुर् विज्ञाय हरि पुंगवाः ॥४-४५-२॥
शूराः च बलवंतः च कृत अस्त्राः च रण आजिरे । काल अभिपन्नाः सीदन्ति यथा वालुक सेतवः ॥३-६९-५०॥
translation: O Lakshmana look at the power of time over all creatures There is nothing too heavy for time. Even those who know the use of arms in war, or are brave or strong enough, cannot withstand the force of time like the barriers built with sand.

raw: स राक्षसगणैर्मुख्यैर्वृतो मन्दोदरीसुतः । निर्ययौ नगरात्तूर्णं कृतान्तबलचोदितः ॥६-९१-११॥
translation: Heroic son of Mandodari, impelled by the force of destiny, departed from the city surrounded by Rakshasas.

raw: महाप्रस्थानम् आसाद्य स्वर् गते तु निशाकरे । माम् निर्दहति संतापो वितर्कैः बहुभिः वृतम् ॥४-६३-४॥
translation: 'Nishakara went on his last journey and attained heaven. Since then many sad thoughts have crisscrossed my mind and I am consumed with those thoughts.

raw: ते भिन्नगात्राः समरे वानराः शपपीडिताः । पेतुर्मथितसङ्कल्पाः सुरैरिव महासुराः ॥६-७३-३५॥
translation: Pierced by arrows in the battle, those Vanaras with their necks broken, giving up hopes of winning, frustrated, fell like the demons oppressed by great gods.

raw: तद्भवान्स्वपुरं यातु रत्नान्यादाय पार्थिव । भरतश्च सहायार्थं पृष्ठतस्ते ऽनुयास्यति ॥७-३८-५॥
translation: Therefore, O King, you may return to your city taking the jewels, and Bharata will follow behind you for assistance.

raw: सुग्रीवो वापि तेजस्वी हरयो ऽपि समागताः । इत्युक्तवति तस्मिंश्च सीता सुरसुतोपमा । उवाच सोकसन्तप्ता हनुमन्तं प्लवङ्गमम् ॥५-३८-५५॥
translation: "Hanuman having spoken this way, Sita, resembling a god's daughter, grieving, thus addressed Hanuman:

raw: नंदिग्रामे जटाम् हित्वा भ्रातृभिः सहितो अनघः । रामः सीताम् अनुप्राप्य राज्यम् पुनः अवाप्तवान् ॥१-१-८९॥
translation: At Nandigrama sinless Rama arrived, met his brothers. They shed their matted locks. With Sita restored he regained his kingdom.

raw: महा मात्र वचः श्रुत्वा रामः दशरथम् तदा । अन्वभाषत वाक्यम् तु विनयज्ञो विनीतवत् ॥२-३७-१॥
translation: On hearing the minister, Rama who knew how to be polite spoke these words to Dasaratha humbly:

raw: एवमुक्तः सुरैर्ब्रह्मा ऽचिन्तयत् पद्मसम्भवः । चिन्तिता चोपतस्थे ऽस्य पार्श्वं देवी सरस्वती ॥७-१०-४१॥
translation: Thus addressed by the gods, Brahma, born from a lotus, pondered, and as he thought, the goddess Saraswati approached his side.

raw: यम् पृष्ठतो अनुगच्चन्ति शतशो अथ सहस्रशः । वृक्षानुद्यम्य सहसा लङ्का रोहणतत्पराः ॥६-२७-४॥
translation: "Standing in attention near Sugriva are hundreds and thousands of warriors holding huge trees aspiring to climb Lanka and controlling the Vanaras at the back prominently and following."

raw: एकाक्षीमेककर्णाम् च कर्णप्रावरणाम् तथा । अकर्णाम् शङ्कुकर्णाम् च मस्तकोच्छ्वासनासिकाम् ॥५-१७-५॥
translation: While Hanuman was eager to observe Sita he saw many shedemons in ugly appearance close by her. One of them was oneeyed, another with a single ear, a third had ears covering the body, yet another had pointed (spikelike) ears, one was breathing through the nose on the head, one had long thin neck, one was hairless another had hair covering like a blanket. One of them had hanging ears on the forehead, another had big hanging lips, still another had long lips hanging up to the chin. So also one had protruding knees, one stunted, one tall, another had lips extending up to her chin, yet another was longfaced and another had long knees. There was one pigmy, one tall, one was humpbacked and another a dwarf.Similarly an ugly looking one, another with gaping mouth, still another with a distorted face, one with yellow eyes and one of deformed face were seen.

raw: एष आशम्सते लंकाम् एको मर्दितुम् ओजसा । येव जाज्वल्यतेऽसौ वै धूमकेतुस्तवाद्य वै ॥६-२८-१७॥
translation: "This monkey is intending to demolish this Lanka single handed. How can you forget about (the task of) setting his tail on fire entrusted by you to Dhoomakethu?"

raw: वत्सला स्वं यथा वत्समुपगूह्य तपस्विनी । परिपप्रच्छ भरतं रुदन्ती शोकलालसा ॥२-८७-८॥
translation: Desolate Kausalya, in deep distress, clasped Bharata out of filial love as if he were her own child, wept and enquired of him:

raw: पुष्पनद्धां वसन्तान्ते मत्तभ्रमरनादिताम् । द्रुतदावाग्निविप्लुष्टां क्लान्तां वनलतामिव ॥२-११४-१२॥
translation: with the melodious humming of intoxicated bees and suddenly shrivelling, ravaged by the fastspreading forest fire.

raw: रजन्यामप्रकाशश्च सन्तापयति चन्द्रमाः । कृष्णरक्तान्तपर्यन्तो यथा लोकस्य सङ्क्षये ॥६-४१-१७॥
translation: "Like at the time of universal dissolution, the moon is not radiant, being surrounded by black and red halo at night and is tormenting."

raw: मुञ्च मुञ्चेति भाषन्तस्तिष्ठतिष्ठेति चासकृत् । मुसलानि सशूलानि सोत्ससर्ज तदार्जुने ॥७-३२-६९॥
translation: Then, Ravana's army repeatedly hurled maces and spears at Arjuna, shouting "release, release" and "stop, stop."

raw: महदद्भुतमाश्चर्यं विदेहस्य पुरातनम् । निर्वृत्तं राजशार्दूल वसिष्ठस्य निमेस्सह ॥७-५८-२॥
translation: O tiger among kings, a great and ancient astonishing event concerning Videha occurred involving Vasishtha and Nimi.

raw: आकारः चाद्यमानो अपि न शक्यो विनिगूहितुम् । बलाद्द् हि विवृणोति एव भावम् अन्तर् गतम् नृणाम् ॥६-१७-६४॥
translation: "Even if one intends to hide in his external form, it is not feasible to keep it concealed. The inner feeling of a man gets revealed even if cleverly hidden."

raw: अपश्यंस्तु न ते सर्वे विशेषमधिकं ततः । स्थापनं चक्रिरे तत्र चातुर्वर्ण्यस्य सम्मतम् ॥७-७४-१४॥
translation: Not seeing any greater distinction among them, all of them then established the approved system of four varnas.

raw: ततस्तमादायतदा स मेनेहरीन्द्रमिन्द्रोपममिन्द्रवीर्यः । अस्मिन् हतेसर्वमिदंहतंस्यात्सराघवंसैन्यमितीन्द्रशत्रुः ॥६-६७-७२॥
translation: Then Kumbhakarna, an enemy of Indra, who was equal to Indra in heroism seizing Sugriva, the Indra of monkeys, who is equal to Indra, thought, 'If Sugriva is killed it is like killing all the army including Rama.'

raw: धनुर्गृहीत्वा तूणी च खड्गं च रुचिरप्रभम् । निक्षिप्य नगरे वीरौ सौमित्रिभरतावुभौ ॥७-७५-९॥
translation: Having taken his bow, quiver, and a beautifully shining sword, and having left both heroes Lakshmana and Bharata in the city, (Rama proceeded).

raw: स त्वं पुरुषशार्दूल धर्मेण सुसमाहितः । शेषं भविष्यं काकुत्स्थ काव्यं रामायणं शृणु ॥७-९८-२०॥
translation: Therefore, O best among men, O Kakutstha, being well-composed and attentive to righteousness, listen to the remaining future events of the Ramayana poem.

raw: सुग्रीवो वानर इन्द्रस् त्वाम् युद्ध अर्थम् अभिवर्तते । महाबलवृतो नित्यम् महाबलपराक्रमः ॥६-२८-४३॥
translation: "In this manner (surrounded by) thousand crore Sankhas, a hundred thousand MahaSankhas, so also by a hundred Vrindas and thousand MahaVrindas, so also by a hundred Padmas and a thousand Mahapadmas, similarly by a hundred Kharvas nay by a Samudra, and similarly by a hundred Oghas and a hundred crore MahaOghas of monkey warriors, accompanied by gallant Vibheeshana and his ministers Sugriva the king of monkeys is ever surrounded by the great army of highly valiant and strong warriors is marching to wage war.

raw: यस्मात्त्वमन्यं वृतवान्मामवज्ञाय पार्थिव । चेतनेन विनाभूतो देहस्तव भविष्यति ॥७-५५-१७॥
translation: "O King, because you have chosen another, disregarding me, your body will become devoid of consciousness."

raw: एवम् वर्ष सहस्राणाम् शतम् वा अहम् त्वया सह । व्यतिक्रमम् न वेत्स्यामि स्वर्गोऽपि हि न मे मतः ॥२-२७-१९॥
translation: Thus living in your company for a thousand years or even a hundred thousand years, I shall not feel the passing of time. I shall not desire even heaven.

raw: न मे तत्र मनस्तापो न मन्युः हरिपुंगव । वागुराभिः च पाशैः च कूटैः च विविधैः नराः ॥४-१८-३७॥
translation: 'O best of monkeys I have no mental agony nor do I regret in this case. Hidden from view or out in the open, people catch animals by means of snares or ropes or through other tricks.

raw: न हि मे काम्क्षितम् राज्यम् सुखमात्मनि वा प्रियम् । यथा निदेशम् कर्तुम् वै तवैव रघुनन्धन ॥२-३४-४५॥
translation: Do not brood. Bestow the kingdom on Bharata. I do not have any desire for the kingdom or pleasure. Nothing is dearer to me than compliance with your order, O Delight of the Raghu race

raw: निह्श्वसन्तम् यथा नागम् रावणम् वानर उत्तमः । आसाद्य परम उद्विग्नः सो अपासर्पत् सुभीतवत् ॥५-१०-१२॥
translation: Having reached Ravana, who was breathing (hissing) like a snake, Hanuman was for a moment frightened and drew away from him as if he was put to terrible fear.

raw: क्व नु वत्स्यति धर्म आत्मा वृक्ष मूलम् उपाश्रितः । सो अत्यन्त सुखितः सूत किम् अशिष्यति राघवः ॥२-५८-५॥
translation: O charioteer Rama is rightous and he is acustoomed to all sorts of comfort. Taking refuge at the foot of a tree how shall he live and what shall he eat?

raw: त्वरया चानयामास पश्चात्तौ श्रोष्यतः प्रियम् । तान्वेश्मनानाभरणैर्यथार्हं प्रतिपूजितान् ॥२-१-४७॥
घोरम् देशम् इमम् प्राप्तौ दैवेन मम चाक्षुषौ । वदतम् कार्यम् इह वाम् किम् अर्थम् च आगतौ युवाम् ॥३-६९-४४॥
गच्छन्नेव महाबाहुर्द्युतिमान् भरतस्तदा । शत्रुघ्नं चाब्रवीद्धृष्टस्तानमात्यांश्च सर्वश: ॥२-९९-८॥
translation: Walking on, the longarmed, effulgent and delighted Bharata said to Satrughna and the ministers surrounding him:

raw: ततस्तलेनाभिहतो महारथः स तस्य पिङ्गाधिपमन्त्रिनिर्जितः । प्रभग्ननीडः परिमुक्तकूबरः पपात भूमौ हतवाजिरम्बरात् ॥५-४७-३२॥
translation: Then hit by Hanuman with his palm, the minister of the copperyeyed Sugriva, the huge chariot seat of Aksha was broken, the wooden frame of the yoke was disjointed, horses were slain and the great chariot fell down from the sky.

raw: ततो हनूमानुत्प्लुत्य हयांत्रिशिरसस्तदा । विददार नखैः क्रुद्धो गजेन्द्रं मृगराडिव ॥६-७०-३७॥
translation: Then Hanuman also jumped up in anger and tore the horse off Trisira just as the lion would tear the lordly elephant with nails.

raw: नक्षत्रेण च सौम्येन पुरस्कृत्याङ्गिरस्सुतम् । भरतः सह सैन्येन कुमाराभ्यां विनिर्ययौ ॥७-१००-२०॥
translation: Bharata, honoring Vashistha (the son of Angiras) and choosing an auspicious constellation, set out with his army and the two princes.

raw: न च धर्म गुणैर् हीनैः कौसल्या आनंद वर्धनः । न च तीक्ष्णो हि भूतानाम् सर्व भूत हिते रतः ॥३-३७-९॥
translation: Rama, the delight of Kausalya, has not forsaken by his father. He has never crossed the limits of dharma. He is not miserly. He has no bad conduct. He is not a slur on the kshatriyas. He does not lack in righteousness. He is not cruel nor is he engaged in doing harm to others.

raw: लङ्काया दुष्प्रवेशत्वाद् दुस्तरत्वान्महोदधेः । सामर्थ्यादात्मनश्चैव मयैतत् समुदीरितम् ॥५-३८-८॥
translation: "Crossing the ocean and entering Lanka are difficult. But I accomplished it. Hence my proposal.

raw: गान्धर्वं वरुणः श्रोतुं यं त्वमाह्वयसे युधि । तत्किं तव वृथा वीर परिश्रम्य गते नृपे । ये तु सन्निहिता वीराः कुमारास्ते पराजिताः ॥७-२३-५२॥
translation: Varuna, whom you challenge in battle, has gone to hear Gandharva music; therefore, O hero, what is the use of your vain exertion when the king is absent, and those princes who were present here have already been defeated?

raw: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमद्युद्धकाण्डे नवतितमः सर्गः ॥ ९० ॥६-९०-५५॥
असिभिः पट्टिशैः शूलैर्गदाभिर्मुसलैर्हुलैः । शक्तिभिस्तीक्ष्णधाराभिर्महद्भिः कूटमुद्गरैः ॥६-९६-२५॥
translation: Then the Rakshasas of terrific looks, and frightening faces holding on shoulders roaring departed with swords, spears, tridents, maces, iron bars, halas, sharp pointed javelins, huge Kutamudgaras, staffs and several discusses, sharp Bhindipalas, Sataghnis and many kinds of excellent weapons.

raw: क्षात्ऺत्रं धर्ममहं त्यक्ष्ये ह्यधर्मं धर्मसंहितम् । क्षुद्रैर्नृशंसैर्लुब्धैश्च सेवितं पापकर्मभि: ॥२-१०९-२०॥
translation: I renounce the socalled kshatriya code of conduct followed by the mean the cruel, the greedy and by men of evil deeds which is unrighteousness under the cloak of righteousness.

raw: स संभ्रमात् त्वरन् राम शन्कितो गौतमम् प्रति । गौतमम् स ददर्श अथ प्रविशंतम् महामुनिम् ॥१-४८-२४॥
तच्छ्रुत्वा भाषितं तस्य रामस्याक्लिष्ट कर्मणः । द्वास्स्थः कुमारावाहूय राघवाय न्यवेदयत् ॥७-८३-१॥
translation: Having heard the words of Rama, whose deeds were effortless, the doorkeeper called the two princes and announced their arrival to Raghava.

raw: आनाययित्वा तनयम् कौसल्याया महा द्युतिम् । स्वयम् एव प्रवेक्ष्यामि वनम् मुनि निषेवितम् ॥२-७४-३१॥
translation: If I fail to bring back the mighty son of Kausalya, I shall enter the forest frequented by ascetics.

raw: बभूव तिमिरम् घोरम् उद्धतम् रोम हर्षणम् । दिशो वा प्रदिशो वा अपि सुव्यक्तम् न चकाशिरे ॥३-२३-८॥
translation: A terrific darkness, spread all over, produced frightening horripilation. Even the four quarters and the intermediary zones were not discernible.

raw: तत् श्रुत्वा निपुणम् सर्वम् भरतः सह मन्त्रिभिः । इन्गुदी मूलम् आगम्य राम शय्याम् अवेक्ष्य ताम् ॥२-८८-१॥
translation: After listening to all that Guha had said, Bharatha reached the foot of the ingudi tree accompanied by his ministers and gazing at Rama's bed, said to all his mothers the magnanimous Rama rested that night here on this ground in that crushed bed.

raw: तम् हि चिन्तयमानायाः शोको अयम् हृदि वर्धते । अदीनाम् इव वेगेन समुद्र सलिलम् महत् ॥२-६२-१९॥
translation: As I think of Rama, my heart swells with sorrow just as the ocean rises with rushing rivers.

raw: कतरेण गमिष्यामि भरद्वाज आश्रमम् गुह । गहनो अयम् भृशम् देशो गन्गा अनूपो दुरत्ययः ॥२-८५-४॥
translation: O Guha this region of Ganga with its dense forest is very difficult to cross. How can I reach the hermitage of Bharadwaja?

raw: ददर्श तं राजपथं दिवि देवपथम् यथा । दध्यक्षतहविर्लाजैर्धूपैरगुरुचम्दनैः ॥२-१७-६॥
translation: Rama beheld the highway resembling the pathway of gods in heaven. Here the crossroads were always worshipped with curd, grains of rice, sacrificial libations, laja or puffed rice, fragrant substances like sandal wood, agaru and garlands of every kind.

raw: तम् तु देशम् अतिक्रम्य शैलोदा नाम निम्नगा । उभयोः तीरयोः तस्याः कीचका नाम वेणवः ॥४-४३-३७॥
translation: 'Passing that region you will reach a mountain stream called Sailoda. On both the banks of the stream are bamboo groves called Kichakas. They waft the siddhas to and from the river. (Kichakas bend forward forming an arch and thus help sages to cross the river.)

raw: इदम् तु नृप शार्दूल पायसम् देव निर्मितम् । प्रजा करम् गृहाण त्वम् धन्यम् आरोग्य वर्धनम् ॥१-१६-१९॥
translation: "O Lion among kings, receive this payasam prepared by gods, conferring progeny, bestowing affluence and improving health.

raw: शुचीनि अभ्यवहार्याणि मूलानि च फलानि च । कांचनानि विमानानि राजतानि गृहाणि च ॥४-५१-५॥
translation: 'To whom do these golden trees resembling the rising Sun belong? For whom are these tasty roots and fruits? Whose are these manystoreyed golden houses with glittering windows adorned with silver lattices encrusted with gems?

raw: पितृमत्यः स्म भद्रम् ते स्वच्छन्दे न वयम् स्थिताः । पितरम् नो वृणीष्व त्वम् यदि नो दास्यते तव ॥१-३३-३॥
translation: We have our father who is dear to us. Hence we do not have freedom to choose. You may ask our father if he is willing to give us (in marriage).

raw: मम संजात रोषस्य मुखम् दृष्ट्वा एव मैथिलि । विद्रवन्ति परित्रस्ताः सुराः शक्र पुरोगमाः ॥३-४८-७॥
translation: O Princess from Mithila, seeing my angry face even gods led by Indra take to their heels in fear.

raw: न अन्यम् नरम् उपस्थातुम् सुराणाम् अपि च ईश्वरम् । न हि राम समः कश्चिद् विद्यते त्रिदशेष्व् अपि ॥५-११-३॥
translation: 'Lovely Sita, being away from Rama, will not sleep, will not eat or drink or adorn herself. How can she approach any other man even if he is the king of gods for there is none equal to Rama even among gods'. Having thus decided, Hanuman strolled about the banquet hall.

raw: रोहि मांसानि च उद्धृत्य पेशी कृत्वा महायशाः । शकुनाय ददौ रामो रम्ये हरित शाद्वले ॥३-६८-३३॥
translation: Tearing the flesh of the deer to pieces and making them into balls, the celebrated Rama laid it on a lovely, green grassy land as offering to the bird.

raw: एवं तौ तु सुसङ्क्रुद्धौ चक्रतुर्युद्धमद्भुतम् । मुहूर्तमभवद्युद्धं तुमुलं रोमहर्षणम् ॥६-१०९-२८॥
translation: Both became furious in that way and the best duel took place for a moment that was fierce and horipulating.

raw: दुहिता वानर इन्द्रस्य कुंजरस्य महात्मनः । मानुषम् विग्रहम् कृत्वा रूप यौवन शालिनी ॥४-६६-१०॥
translation: 'She was the daughter of a great king of monkeys called Kunjara. That young and beautiful lady had assumed a lustrous human form decked with wonderful garlands, ornaments and silk clothes and was roving on top of the mountain which appeared like a proud raincloud.

raw: तदिदं मानुषं मन्ये प्राप्तं निस्संशयं भयम् । जीवितान्तकरं घोरं रक्षसां रावणस्य च ॥६-९५-२९॥
translation: "Fearlessness of death from human beings attained by Ravana in this way was no doubt terrific to Rakshasas and Ravana."

raw: तान्समालिङ्ग्य बाहुभ्यां विष्टब्धाः केचिदुच्छ्रुताः । देवैस्तु शस्त्रसम्भिन्ना मम्रिरे च निशाचराः ॥७-२८-४१॥
translation: Some night-wanderers, embracing others with their arms, were paralyzed and raised high, while others, pierced by the weapons of the gods, died.

raw: तस्योग्ररूपस्योग्र त्वं दण्डमाज्ञातुमर्हसि । सीता संभाषिता येन तद्वनं च विनाशितम् ॥५-४२-२०॥
translation: "Your highness should take severe action on that person of fierce appearance with whom Sita dared to speak, and by whom the garden is ruined.

raw: हृष्टः सौहृदम् आलम्ब्य पर्यष्वजत पीडितम् । ततो हनूमान् संत्यज्य भिक्षु रूपम् अरिन्दमः ॥४-५-१३॥
प्रतिगृह्य तु ताम् पूजाम् ऋषि दत्ताम् प्रतापवान् । रामम् दाशरथिम् रामो जामदग्न्यो अभ्यभाषत ॥१-७४-२४॥
translation: Valiant Parasurama, son of Jamadagni, having accepted the homage offered by the saints addressed Rama, son of Dasaratha and said: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे चतुस्सप्ततितमस्सर्ग:।। Thus ends the seventyfourth sarga of Balakanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.

raw: अयम् हि सर्व भूतानाम् मान्यः तु नर सत्तमः । अस्मासु च गतः प्रीतिम् रामः पर पुरम् जयः ॥४-४३-९॥
translation: 'This Rama who can conquer the capitals of enemies is great. He loves and is loved by all living beings including ourselves.

raw: प्रसीद लंकेश्वर राक्षसेन्द्रलंकाम् प्रसन्नो भव साधु गच्छ । त्वम् स्वेषु दारेषु रमस्व नित्यम्रामः स भार्यो रमताम् वनेषु ॥३-३१-४९॥
translation: O lord of Lanka, chief of the demons, be pleased to return to Lanka and enjoy yourself in the company of your wives. Let Rama enjoy with his wife in the forest.

raw: पूर्णे चतुर्दशे वर्षे पञ्चम्यां लक्ष्मणाग्रजः । भरद्वाजश्रमं प्राप्य ववन्दे नियतो मुनिम् ॥६-१२७-१॥
translation: After the fourteenth year of exile, on the fifth day of the bright half of lunar month Sri Rama and Lakshmana reached Bharadwaja's hermitage. They bent their heads down (as a mark of respect) and offered salutations.

raw: ततो विष्णुमयं देवं पूजयन्ति स्म देवताः । साध्या मरुद्गणाश्चैव सेन्द्राः साग्निपुरोगमाः ॥७-११०-१३॥
translation: Then, the gods, including the Sadhyas, the Maruts, Indra, and those led by Agni, worshipped the deity who had become one with Vishnu.

raw: हतान् मन्त्रिसुतान् बुद्ध्वा वानरेण महात्मना । रावणः संवृताकारश्चकार मतिमुत्तमाम् ॥५-४६-१॥
translation: Coming to know that the seven sons of the ministers were slain by the great vanara, Ravana, who had concealed his feelings of agony thought of a good plan.
